There are limits on the access granted to those supervising teen accounts.

Parents and guardians cannot read private messages, see searches or viewing history, post as their teen, or access the account.

According to recent reports, notably, X says both sides must agree before supervision is permitted. The arrangement ends automatically when the teenager hits their 18th birthday.

AMD Specific Patches for Llama.cpp

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Devnull

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • tl;dr — I recommend using llama-cpp-rdna-boosts if you have an AMD graphics card.
  • In a recent development, as of November 2026, an explosion in the number of bespoke inference engines has taken place.
  • According to recent reports, the rationale isn’t that those options are bad, but merely that they are generalist engines, optimized for no particular hardware and with a focus on broad compatibility.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

tl;dr — I recommend using llama-cpp-rdna-boosts if you have an AMD graphics card. It’s lean, and increased my token generation from 35 to 55 tokens/second, and my prefill from 700 to 1300 tokens per second. YMMV.

In a recent development, as of November 2026, an explosion in the number of bespoke inference engines has taken place. Many of them take inspiration from the engines that enabled much of the LLM inference up 'til now: llama.cpp, SGLang, vLLM, etc.

According to recent reports, the rationale isn’t that those options are bad, but merely that they are generalist engines, optimized for no particular hardware and with a focus on broad compatibility. Others feel the development pace of those engines have slowed down, and with the help of LLMs, they can move faster on their own.

Some examples of these newly introduced inference engines* are Strata, Basalt, RustingStrata, etc….

These new forks generally all have a few things in common:.

… and the results are stunning! Strata is able to run a heavily-quantized model of Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, a 180B parameter model, on a 16GB VRAM graphics card, and 16GB system RAM, and have it generate tokens at a surprisingly high rate.

In and of itself those three things are not red flags (the second is concerning, of course, but it may be SOP in a year’s time — who knows!), but as these projects have evolved, that relentless chase toward higher token generation speeds has taken an unfortunate turn, in that the optimizations are less about hardware-specific changes, but more about changing how the model thinks so that it goes brrr faster.

Recent findings suggest that strata specifically has taken to preferring to poll experts loaded in VRAM even if other experts (pushed to system RAM/disk) would have been normally chosen. This is just one example, but certainly not the last.

That said, I was fortunate to stumble upon yet another project that promised improvements, delivered, and was more aligned with my software development philosophy.

Recent findings suggest that enter llama-cpp-rdna-boosts. It is a repository that contains a minimal set of changes that you apply against a pinned commit of llama.cpp. It is in essence a fork, but one whose changeset is continually re-applied to newer versions of llama.cpp. It contains AMD-specific improvements that drastically improve prefill and token-generation speeds.

According to recent reports, if you have ROCm libraries installed on your system, you can build the image yourself. I didn’t want to mess with that, so I used the pre-built images published.

podman pull ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1.

This sets up an image that you can run sandboxed via podman to launch the inference server:.

My actual launch script passes a few additional flags, but those are the important lines.

I imagine upgrading would be pulling a fresh image down, though I have not tried this yet.

On my setup, an AMD R9700 connected to my laptop via an eGPU interface, this improved prefill and token generation rates when running ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF (Q6_K_L) with MTP enabled:.

Strata and its ilk were always promising the moon and it was never clear what steps they took to make that happen. I’m very much looking forward to what the rdna-boosts community come up with next.

* It’s worth noting that between these two groups, vllm-radiance made an appearance, which was a fork of vLLM with AMD-specific patches. I tried this too, but the build steps were so onerous and vLLM so overbuilt for my specific use case (1 machine, 1 developer), that I abandoned it and went back to vanilla llama.cpp.

Uber, Nuro and Lucid Begin Fully Driverless Testing With Their Luxury Robotaxi

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (601 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies remarked Tuesday.
  • Recent findings suggest that the partnership, announced in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles.
  • Now, the partnership is ready to take its next big step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies remarked Tuesday.

Recent findings suggest that the partnership, announced in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles. Autonomous rides take place aboard the Lucid Gravity robotaxi, which I had the opportunity to see first at a CES showcase in January (in the form of a “production intent design”), and then on the road this summer, with a safety driver behind the wheel.

Now, the partnership is ready to take its next big step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies said. They plan to launch commercial robotaxi operations in the first quarter of 2027 in the San Francisco Bay Area, before expanding to Houston later next year. Lucid will begin manufacturing the first vehicles designed specifically for the commercial launch fleet “in the coming weeks.” Uber prepares to deploy around 35,000 Lucid vehicles equipped with the Nuro Driver in the coming years in “dozens” of cities.

According to recent reports, “Removing the safety operator from behind the wheel is an vital milestone in our partnership with Nuro and Lucid, and a testament to all three partners’ focus on executing against our shared roadmap,” Samarth Kejriwal, Uber’s global head of autonomous mobility, said in a statement. “As we prepare for our first driverless passenger rides in the coming months, we’ll be working closely together to refine our operations, infrastructure and the in-cabin experience to ensure a safer, more comfortable ride.”.

Nuro notes it’s been conducting “round-the-clock autonomous testing of the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area and Houston” since December 2025, with a safety driver in the vehicle who can take over if needed.

In May, Nuro received a California Public Utilities Commission Drivered Pilot Permit, giving the firm the green light to conduct pilot testing for an autonomous passenger service with a safety driver. Nuro also received a California Department of Motor Vehicles Driverless Testing Permit in April, allowing it to test self-driving vehicles without a safety driver.

Industry observers note that uber’s partnership with Nuro and Lucid is just one of dozens it has with other AV companies, including Waymo, Zoox, Avride, Wayve and May Mobility. Adding driverless options to an app that’s likely already on someone’s phone could increase their chances of giving the experience a try — despite the trepidation many people have about self-driving vehicles.

Sources indicate that the Lucid Gravity robotaxi can seat up to six passengers, unlike rides from Waymo and Zoox that seat up to four. It has plenty of legroom and ample space for luggage in the back. The vehicle’s sensor suite is equipped with cameras, lidar sensors and radars for autonomous navigation.

Industry observers note that it’s been a big year for autonomous vehicles, and it appears 2027 will be no different. The rapid expansion of AVs comes amid heightened scrutiny. Last week, the California DMV banned Waymo’s robotaxis from state freeways after a series of high-profile incidents — after which Waymo paused all of its freeway rides. Waymo, the largest player in the AV space, has been involved in a number of other safety incidents as it expands to more cities. Over the years, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has launched investigations into other AV companies, including Zoox and Tesla.

It’s against this landscape — and the full-speed-ahead race toward autonomy — that Nuro, Uber and Lucid will soon publicly debut their own robotaxi.

Google Wallet comes to your iPhone – but without this feature

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (477 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time.
  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • Sources indicate that the new Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the new Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

Sources indicate that the new Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app users on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

Recent findings suggest that there used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the upcoming Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Recent findings suggest that agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

It has been revealed that the Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of new tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Industry observers note that along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is out now, and while it might be one of the most anticipated game releases of the year, not everyone likes the series or is interested in it. If you want to play something more fantastical, Xbox Game Pass has you covered with High on Life 2, Hela: Of Mice and Magic and more soon.

Xbox Game Pass, a CNET Editors’ Choice award winner, offers a wide selection of games you can play on your Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox One and PC or mobile device for as little as $10 per month. With a higher-tier Game Pass Ultimate subscription ($23 per month), you can access hundreds of titles, including latest ones on release day.

Here’s everything Microsoft is adding to Xbox Game Pass soon.

Latest to Game Pass Premium. Previously added to Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

This sequel to the 2022 first-person shooter High on Life has players once again traveling throughout space and taking down bad guys with the help of an arsenal of talking guns. The game comes from Squanch Games, which was founded by a co-creator of the Rick and Morty series, so expect some raunchy humor and antics.

This prequel to the Outlast series retains the horror of the other games and adds a Cold War-era twist. You’ve been abducted and are subjected to medical and psychological experiments. To survive, you have to fight and evade other test subjects in a massive facility run by the shady Murkoff Corporation.

According to recent reports, you’ve seen mice, right? Small, cute creatures that scamper around and are sometimes kept as pets? Well, in this co-op game, you get to see the world through the eyes of one of those critters. You’ll solve puzzles, explore landscapes inspired by Northern Sweden and take in a heartwarming story told via fuzzy friends.

While Microsoft is adding several games to Game Pass, it’s also removing eight others on Nov. 30. So you still have some time to complete your main campaign or any side quests before you’ll have to buy these games separately.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've slept on all kinds of mattresses for my job at Tom's Guide but the firm, supportive comfort of the Siena Signature has to rate among my favorites. Back to its lowest price with a queen mattress just $279 at Siena in the Black Friday sales, this affordable mattress eases back pain for under $300.

The Siena isn't merely a budget-friendly pick — it's one of the best mattresses we've tested. The firm foams hold the body straight, which I found reduces the pressure that's built on my spine after a day hunched over my desk.

Always under $400 for a queen, at this price you're not going to get the durability of a more expensive mattress. For beds that'll last you 5+ years, our Black Friday mattress sales live blog has plenty of options at great prices. But for comfort that won't break the bank, the Siena is my pick of the Black Friday mattress deals.

Industry observers note that the Siena Signature has dropped back to its cheapest price of the year, with a queen now only $279 (it was $349 a few weeks ago) and a twin just $169. That's incredible value for one of the best memory foam mattresses, and you get a 180-night trial plus a 10-year warranty. It's highly unlikely we'll see further price drops so now is the time to shop.

Our Siena Signature mattress review: ★★★★.

The Siena didn't have an easy ride into our best mattress guide. To be crowned the best cheap mattress we've put it through our rigorous lab-based mattress testing methodology as well as subjecting it to an extended 10 month at-home testing period.

During that time the Siena continuously impressed with its full-body support. One of the best firm mattresses you can buy online, it holds the spine lifted and aligned, reducing back pain for stomach and back sleepers.

As someone with a tendency to hunch over my laptop, I need a mattress that helps take strain off my spine. The Siena delivered, as the firm foams held me straight from neck to tailbone, allowing my muscles to unwind.

It also has phenomenal edge support (some of the best we've tested). You can sit, lie, or push against the side without ever feeling like you're slipping.

Industry observers note that the motion isolation is also excellent, as the dense foams stop movement from traveling across the bed. When someone jumped in on one side of the mattress, I could hardly feel them on the other.

And finally, temperature regulation. This often trips up cheap all-foam beds but the Siena is one of the best cooling mattresses on a budget we've tested. While it doesn't feel cool to the touch it stays at a constant temperature, even during warm nights.

However, as a firm mattress, the Siena doesn't have enough cushioning for many side sleepers. If that sounds like a problem, we have a solution.

I slept on the Zinus Green Tea and in my opinion, the best way to sum it up is "marshmallow".   • The tech giant recently filed for bankruptcy and is now offering all of its assets for sale, including the contents of user chat sessions.
  • Recent findings suggest that character․AI had long come under fire for its extremely irresponsible attitude to privacy and safety.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, with most AI chatbots using your interactions as training data, we’ve previously cautioned against sharing sensitive personal details with them, highlighting the much stronger privacy protections offered by Apple. If you ever needed evidence of the importance of this, the Character․ai mess provides it.

The tech giant recently filed for bankruptcy and is now offering all of its assets for sale, including the contents of user chat sessions. Some 42 state attorneys general are trying to block this, but it’s unclear whether they will succeed ….

Recent findings suggest that character․AI had long come under fire for its extremely irresponsible attitude to privacy and safety. Last summer, it was accused of harvesting mental health data from underage consumers, and in May of this year it faced a lawsuit after its chatbots were found to be pretending to be licensed doctors. The firm filed for bankruptcy last month.

A group of 42 attorneys general are trying to block the chatbot company from auctioning off users’ chat histories and other sensitive information […] “Nothing in the agreement restricts what the buyer may do with the data after closing, including selling it,” the AGs say in a court filing […].

According to recent reports, “Character․AI’s initiative to auction off its platform, including the IP addresses and private chats histories of its users — many of them children — with zero protection for those users is appalling,” California Attorney General Rob Bonta mentioned in a statement. “If this sale goes through, users’ sensitive data would go into the hands of a buyer even though Character․AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold.”.

The chat histories reportedly include conversations in which AI characters drew both adults and children into explicit sexual conversations.

Siri AI interactions are handled on-device wherever possible. Where this isn’t possible, Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers are used, with guarantees that no data is stored or linked to your Apple account. Apple has designed the system in such a way that its privacy claims can be independently verified by security researchers.

Industry observers note that when a user makes a request, Apple Intelligence analyzes whether it can be processed on device. For more complex requests, it can draw on Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy and security of your iPhone into the cloud. With Private Cloud Compute, only the data that is relevant to your request is processed on Apple silicon servers, before being removed.

The data being processed in Private Cloud Compute is not stored or made accessible to Apple. It is processed only to fulfill your request, after which point the results are returned securely to your device and are not retained by Private Cloud Compute. Independent privacy and security researchers can inspect the code that runs on Apple silicon servers that enable Private Cloud Compute to verify this privacy promise at any time.

Apple also recently introduced a safe way to ask an AI questions about your health. Data sources used are limited to the same platforms used by healthcare professionals, with links to peer-reviewed clinical citations. Apple guarantees that your chat sessions are not used for AI training with no retention of either questions or answers.

90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider.
  • Fresh data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.
  • In a recent development, also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

Fresh data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

In a recent development, also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost.

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

It has been revealed that employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

According to recent reports, “As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

The report shows how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams.

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse said, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”.

Greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson remarked.

What we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson remarked Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”.

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he remarked.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor.

Recent findings suggest that it’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report noted.

According to recent reports, but how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

“The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report shows 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the organization, human or AI,” Samson mentioned. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”.

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead.

According to recent reports, samson said that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

“For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson said. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”.

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most important decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse stated.

In a recent development, A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more important tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside.

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse said.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

Industry observers note that “When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson said. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Massive holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a blueprint to protect your package from porch pirates.
  • Sources indicate that CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts.
  • Sources indicate that but leaving your packages up for grabs could be a major risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Massive holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a blueprint to protect your package from porch pirates.

Sources indicate that CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts. This year, the average package value is $276.24, and 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or caught an attempted theft within the past year. Yet 20% of US adults don’t use security devices due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees.

Sources indicate that but leaving your packages up for grabs could be a major risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered. On the other hand, some bad actors don’t seem to mind being caught in the act on home security cameras, so are they really enough to deter bad actors? And what more can you do to protect your deliveries?

CNET’s findings show that some US adults have dealt with porch theft firsthand: 8% had packages meant for themselves or their households stolen within the past year, and 5% had a delivered gift stolen. Very few (1%) caught a theft in the act on a video doorbell or security camera.

Meanwhile, many US adults know someone who fell victim to package theft — 13% know a neighbor or community member who had a package stolen within the past year, and 12% know someone who doesn’t live in their community who has.

Industry observers note that “Close to a third of our respondents are personally acquainted with package theft, which is still a high number compared to other problems like break-ins,” mentioned CNET’s senior home security editor, Tyler Lacoma. “Thieves generally look for crimes of opportunity, and few things are easier than a package left on a doorstep, especially if nobody is home.”.

Surprisingly, most US adults (72%) haven’t experienced package theft or know anyone who has.

Even though the percentages above may seem low, Lacoma said that package theft typically increases during the holidays when thieves know more deliveries are likely, and new porch theft tactics are always on the horizon.

In a recent development, there are reports of thieves trying Wi-Fi jamming to disable live security camera footage while they steal packages. And findings show that some are installing spy cams in high-value neighborhoods to learn your home’s layout and habits to take your packages shortly after they’re delivered. In recent years, pirates have even tracked shipping labels for high-value tech, like iPhones, to steal the package within minutes of arrival.

It has been revealed that so while the majority of US adults haven’t fallen victim, that shouldn’t be a sign to shrug off the concern or relax your home security measures. Instead, now’s the time to blueprint how to safely store your packages if they’re delivered while you’re away.

Online shopping and deliveries to your door can be a convenient way to check off holiday wish lists, but the average package value this holiday season is less than last year. CNET found that US adults plan to have an average of $276.24 in holiday packages delivered during this holiday season. That’s $23.82 less than last year’s average of $300.06.

According to recent reports, by generation, Millennials also have a lower estimated average package value than last year, with an average of $227.25, compared to their 2025 package value of $307.47 — an $80.22 difference, while Gen Z’s package value is only about $7 less than last year. But any package’s value is still worth taking precautions to help prevent it from being stolen.

Lacoma has thoughts on why that might be. In short, lower spending could mean fewer packages.

“I wonder if people have also simply gotten fewer packages in general this year due to tariffs, inflation and tech prices. That could pull these numbers down,” mentioned Lacoma. But there’s a high chance that could be the case considering CNET’s 2026 annual holiday survey, which found that US adult tech spending is down to $808 — which is $123 less than last year’s average of $931.

Recent findings suggest that thieves may not always know what’s in boxes they’re stealing but they’re willing to take a chance. We asked US adults which items were stolen in package thefts in the past year to give you a sense of what’s at risk.

Among the items stolen, apparel and accessories were the most common goods stolen (40%). That’s followed by toys and games (23%). Then there are everyday home basics, like decor, cookware and small appliances (19%).

But personal tech devices and accessories are still among the items stolen. Small accessories like phone chargers and cases are most common (16%) among tech-related packages stolen. They are followed by audio gadgets like headphones and Bluetooth speakers, along with streaming devices and soundbars (11%, respectively).

Still, more costly tech like gaming consoles (10%), computers and laptops (9%) and smart home devices (6%) are among devices stolen.

In a recent development, you shouldn’t leave your packages up to chance. That’s why Lacoma recommends a few safer options to ensure your packages are stored securely after they’re delivered, even beyond keeping an eye on your doorbell or security camera. Instead, keep your packages out of sight with tactics like a delivery box with a code or key or ask for an in-garage delivery.

Recent findings suggest that “Delivery boxes have reached a newly introduced level of popularity in recent years as an effective way to stop porch pirates completely. However, Amazon’s Key service that delivers to your garage is an alternative,” said Lacoma. “Either way, you’ll need to trust delivery people to handle your shipments, unless you want to arrange for pickup at a nearby shipping center, which some people like to combine with other holiday errands.”.

If you don’t want to install a new security feature, try scheduling your packages to arrive when you know you’re home, requiring a signature from someone you trust or changing your delivery location to a pickup spot, like UPS’ Hold for Pick-Up locations or Amazon Lockers.

According to recent reports, home surveillance, like outdoor security cameras and video doorbells, can deter package thieves who don’t want to risk getting caught on camera. But US adults have mixed feelings about their effectiveness in protecting against package theft.

In a recent development, there are two deterrents that are keeping US adults from having security devices — cost and privacy. Findings show that 20% of US adults lack home security measures due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees. That’s followed by 9% who don’t want to use cameras because of privacy concerns.

“Fortunately, the right home security picks can solve both these problems,” remarked Lacoma. “Brands like Tapo, Eufy, Aqara and even Google Nest offer package detection and alerts for free, so you don’t have to worry about extra fees.”.

In a recent development, if you’re looking for a camera that’s off-the-grid, consider the Arlo Go 2. It’s an LTE camera, so it uses a cellular data connection instead of Wi-Fi. It still finds a signal, supports app operation and live video viewing. If you’re looking for a power-over-Ethernet camera that uses a cable connection, the Reolink Duo 3 is a good choice.

Recent findings suggest that lacoma added that many companies also offer ways to use local video storage and local AI detection so nothing is stored in the cloud. There are also features, such as customizable privacy zones, to minimize privacy concerns when used with the right precautions.

Among all US adults, only 14% have security devices with a monthly subscription that lets them save or playback video. By comparison, 12% have security devices but no subscription.

In a recent development, those percentages could be low for a few reasons, including the overall perception of how helpful surveillance and security really are against porch theft. Eleven percent of US adults don’t think security devices deter porch thefts. It’s a valid concern since 4% fell victim to package theft or an attempted theft despite having security devices. And some US adults (9%) use security devices to get proof of a theft after the fact — not to prevent it.

But that doesn’t mean you should ignore the possibility of package theft — especially during the holidays. Even if you don’t want to install cameras or upcoming security devices, make a plan to protect your packages and avoid the headache of package theft over the holidays.

“Remember, the simple presence of a security camera is enough to make many thieves look elsewhere – interviews have confirmed it,” said Lacoma. “And with today’s phone alerts about package detection, you can usually check on a package only seconds after it appears, or bring up footage if it unexpectedly vanishes, letting you take action fast. Latest practices like delivery boxes or in-garage delivery help address risks in concrete ways, too.”.

Recent findings suggest that CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,016 adults. Fieldwork was undertaken between Oct. 23–27, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus).

The $75 billion figure was calculated by multiplying the average value of deliveries each US adult expects to receive by the 2025 US population of adults ages 18 and over calculated by the US Census Bureau.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero.
  • In a recent development, the thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use.
  • Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero. The $399 Flipper One is a pocket Linux computer focused on networking, with delivery estimated for July 2027. But it isn’t simply an updated version of the Flipper Zero. It’s a very different animal and a much more serious bit of kit.

In a recent development, the thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use. You could fire it up and turn the volume down on the TV at your parents’ place, see the radio waves coming from your car’s key fob, and copy hotel room key cards.

Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.

It has been revealed that it could do a lot, there wasn’t a steep learning curve, and you didn’t need to buy anything else. Did the fake videos on TikTok from people claiming they could change the prices at gas stations (I wish!) or start cars remotely help make the Zero more popular?

Industry observers note that unfortunately, yes. But what made it successful was that it packed a lot of power into a package that was small, fun, affordable, and easy to use.

If the Flipper Zero, with its NFC, RFID, sub-GHz, and IR, was kindergarten, the Flipper One is a college degree: a pocket Linux computer focused on networking.

This is reflected in the price. You can pick up a Zero for $169, while the Flipper One is $399.

What this buys you is the Flipper One base computer with a 256 × 144 grayscale LCD, Rockchip RK3576 8-core ARM SoC with NPU, a low-power MCU for handling the LCD and user interface, 8GB of LPDDR5 RAM, 64GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a microSD slot.

If that $399 feels like a lot, it’s worth keeping in mind that, according to Flipper, the price only covers production costs and that the RAM and UFS storage account for at least half of the total hardware cost.

If you think this is a lot, you could spend a lot more. Adding a LoRa, SDR, or 5G module will push the total up a lot higher. And if you want all three modules, you’re looking at $759 for the Flipper One Ultimate Bundle.

Also: The Flipper One is the Linux cyberdeck I wish my Raspberry Pi could be.

According to recent reports, the reception has been strong enough that pledges have flown past the $300,000 goal that Flipper initially set, with over 24,000 backers pledging over $13 million. Close to 5,300 backers have gone for the Ultimate Bundle, compared to just over 4,300 choosing the bare Flipper One.

This suggests that backers really want the radio capabilities that this newly introduced platform offers.

If you want one, this crowdfunding run is a good time to get one because it’s a Kickstarter Special slashing 25% off an estimated retail price of $550.

The response over on Reddit has been a little more subdued, with some being taken aback by the price of the Zero’s bigger sibling.

Also: 7 useful things I can do with my Flipper Zero – as someone who’s used it for years.

As someone who homebrews a lot of electronics, I’m going to say that the price is justified, and this project goes far beyond something you could put together with a Raspberry Pi and some code.

The Flipper One campaign runs until Dec. 17, 2026, with delivery estimated for July 2027.

Keep in mind that this is a Kickstarter pledge, not a purchase, and that rewards aren’t guaranteed. Flipper also says on the Kickstarter page that component shortages are the biggest risk to the project and that they “could cause significant delays to production and delivery.” It also says that if RAM prices continue to rise, it cannot “rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.”.

Also: Is the Flipper Zero the best multi-tool for hacking?

And the good news here is that I’ve seen several analysts predicting that RAM prices will begin to go down in 2027 as demand eases off.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Tuesday, Bambu Lab took the wraps off its third-generation 3D printer, the P3C.
  • The big deal here is the introduction of the Swaptek 7-tool changer, which allows you to switch to a different color or material in just 6 seconds, preventing you from having to stop and clean the nozzle every time.
  • Recent findings suggest that the tool changer technology also allows you to mix different materials with less of a fuss, so you can use a typical rigid plastic and something like a flexible rubber in a single pass without stopping.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Tuesday, Bambu Lab took the wraps off its third-generation 3D printer, the P3C. It brings to the mainstream the firm’s “tool changer” technology, which was previously reserved for higher-end, flagship models like the $2,500 H3C. Given the P3C costs less than half the bigger model, it might be the perfect gift to get your favorite 3D printing hobbyist for Black Friday.

The big deal here is the introduction of the Swaptek 7-tool changer, which allows you to switch to a different color or material in just 6 seconds, preventing you from having to stop and clean the nozzle every time. The technology produces significantly less waste and allows you to create faster prints.

Recent findings suggest that the tool changer technology also allows you to mix different materials with less of a fuss, so you can use a typical rigid plastic and something like a flexible rubber in a single pass without stopping. It can switch between different nozzle sizes in one job. You can switch between  0.2 mm, 0.4 mm, 0.6 mm and 0.8 mm midprint.

Industry observers note that the P3C ships with an integrated sealed AMS 3P filament management system that can store up to seven spools, each of which is on an independent feed path to the printer. You can also connect up to four external AMS units, supporting up to 22 colors.

Recent findings suggest that the P3C is more than just a 3D printer. The Swaptek system supports interchangeable craft tools, letting you cut, draw or emboss on materials.

According to recent reports, bambu Lab also included a few features that make the P3C more approachable to newcomers. The P3C provides full-auto calibration, automatically aligning nozzle offsets and multi-tool heads so you don’t have to do it yourself. There’s also a built-in AI monitoring system that can detect issues like nozzle clogs and purge-bin jams early on. A newly introduced health management system will no longer spit out vague or obscure errors when something goes wrong. Instead, the new system will explain the issue in plain language and provide step-by-step troubleshooting right on the screen.

Sources indicate that CNET’s 3D printing expert, James Bricknell, hasn’t been able to test Bambu Labs’ latest model yet but is excited about it. “While the P3C didn’t arrive in time for a hands-on, it’s built with the same design language and hardware support as the recently released H3C. If it is anywhere near as good, and I think that’s likely, it’ll be at the top of any serious 3D printing enthusiast’s wish list.”.

The P3C 3D printer AMS combo is available now worldwide for $1,149. The combo includes the printer, AMS 3P as well as 5 0.4mm standard PrintTools. Two slots are left open for you to customize. This combo option comes with virtually everything you need to get started printing your works of art and more.

Rocket Lab Stock Just Fell to Its Lowest Price in About a Year. Is It a Buy Now?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (837 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that rocket Lab (RKLB +2.26%) stock fell about 7% on Wednesday, Nov.
  • The growth stock had closed above $66 just two weeks before, soon after Rocket Lab's third-quarter results, and about a third of that value has vanished since.
  • Sources indicate that but the business behind the stock is far bigger than it was the last time shares traded this low.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 26, 2026 at 10:23AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Rocket Lab ›.

Sources indicate that rocket Lab (RKLB +2.26%) stock fell about 7% on Wednesday, Nov. 25, to roughly $43 as I write. The drop left shares at their lowest price since early December 2025 and over 70% below their May 27 record close of $150.23.

The growth stock had closed above $66 just two weeks before, soon after Rocket Lab's third-quarter results, and about a third of that value has vanished since.

Sources indicate that but the business behind the stock is far bigger than it was the last time shares traded this low. What hasn't changed is that Neutron, the reusable rocket behind Rocket Lab's long-term growth prepares, hasn't yet flown.

The last time Rocket Lab stock traded this low, in early December 2025, the firm's revenue for the previous four quarters came to around $555 million. For the last four quarters, it's about $882 million, almost 60% more. Growth has sped up, too. Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 climbed 73% from a year earlier to a record $268 million, after growing 36% in the fourth quarter of 2025. And management expects fourth-quarter revenue of $270 million to $290 million, which at the midpoint would be 56% above the year-ago quarter -- still fast, though slower than the third quarter's rate.

In a recent development, the share count grew, too, but far more slowly. Rocket Lab sold around $3.9 billion in new stock through September, partly to pay for its pending purchase of satellite operator Iridium Communications. Counting preferred stock that converts to common shares, it had about 15% more shares at the end of September than at the end of 2025.

In a recent development, that leaves much more revenue behind each share. At roughly $43, Rocket Lab is valued at about $29 billion, which comes to 33 times the revenue it took in over the last year. At the same share price in early December 2025, the stock traded at more than 40 times sales.

Still, 33 times sales is a high valuation for a business that isn't profitable yet, and I think much of that price depends on Neutron.

Rocket Lab now has 16 Neutron missions booked before the rocket's first flight, and half of them were signed in the third quarter alone, for over $515 million.

But at least six of those eight latest missions aren't scheduled until late 2028 or later. Radar-satellite company ICEYE's three releases start in late 2028, Muon Space's two are set for 2029 and 2030, and Starcloud's is booked for 2029.

Recent findings suggest that rocket Lab expects only around a third of its $3.6 billion total backlog (signed work it hasn't yet counted as revenue) to become revenue within 12 months. Neutron's far-off missions likely make up a massive part of the rest.

It has been revealed that neutron's first launch, meanwhile, is expected in 2027. Before Rocket Lab picks a specific date, it still needs to put together the rocket's first-stage tank and finish pressure and cryogenic (super-cold) testing, according to its last quarterly report.

In a recent development, neutron has to fly first, and even then its early missions might not make money. In the third quarter, Rocket Lab recorded a forward loss reserve (an expected loss booked ahead of time) on the vehicle for Neutron's second flight, because the rocket is still so early in development.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Recent findings suggest that until Neutron flies regularly, the losses will likely keep coming. Rocket Lab lost $18 million in the third quarter on a non-GAAP (adjusted) basis, measured by earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA). That was smaller than its $26 million loss a year earlier, and management expects another loss of $14 million to $20 million in the fourth quarter.

On the third-quarter earnings call, CFO Adam Spice remarked capital spending should stay high as Neutron heads toward production, but he expects adjusted EBITDA to go positive within six months of the rocket's first successful test flight.

In a recent development, I think it can be, for investors willing to wait for Neutron. Each share now comes with much more revenue than it did at this price a year ago, and customers keep booking Neutron debuts. But Neutron still has to show it can fly, then fly often. And a stock that shed a third of its value over two weeks might swing just as hard again. I'd consider buying in stages instead of all at once.

Your Google AI mode searches can stay private now with ‘temporary threads’ – here’s how

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (609 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends.
  • Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.
  • Industry observers note that upcoming to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends. Now Google has jumped on board this bandwagon with its AI Mode searches.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.

Industry observers note that upcoming to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

According to recent reports, this option is presently rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

Try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

Industry observers note that hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a new thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s newly introduced Skills.

Certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:.

Industry observers note that are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google says:.

“Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google said on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”.

Google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

For those reasons, you should still be cautious about the information you share even in a temporary thread. But certainly, this option provides greater privacy and protection than a regular AI Mode search.

ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

Industry observers note that I’m glad to see Google finally offering this option through its AI Mode searches. This marks the second privacy-friendly development in recent days from the search giant. On Tuesday, Google announced that it would be rolling out latest settings through which you could opt out of AI model training without losing access to your chat history.

#131230. A Human and an AI Model (Apparently) Solved the Riemann Hypothesis: What it Means for Future of Math

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2174 w)

A Human and an AI Model (Apparently) Solved the Riemann Hypothesis: What it Means for Future of Math

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2174 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Riemann Hypothesis is one of math’s oldest and most famous unsolved problems.
  • Alpöge made the announcement on Friday in a four-page document (PDF) on his personal web page.
  • According to recent reports, “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge said in the announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Riemann Hypothesis is one of math’s oldest and most famous unsolved problems. It was originally put forward as a problem in 1859 by Bernhard Riemann, and professional and amateur mathematicians alike have made thousands of attempts to solve it. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge has apparently solved the problem with the help of AI, showing that in the battle of humans versus AI, the real winner might be both of them working together.

Alpöge made the announcement on Friday in a four-page document (PDF) on his personal web page.

According to recent reports, “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge said in the announcement. “In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too.”.

The actual hypothesis itself isn’t the biggest deal since all it does is make it easier to see the distribution of prime numbers. However, math didn’t come to a screeching halt just because the hypothesis hadn’t been proven. There are hundreds of other math theorems along with algorithms and cryptographic encryption methods that operate based on the assumption that the Riemann Hypothesis is true.

In a recent development, the Riemann Hypothesis is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute’s seven Millennium Problems for this very reason. If Alpöge really did solve the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude’s help, it would remove a metaphorical logjam that’s been gumming up the works for over a century and a half. Most of those hundreds of math theorems would be proven as true overnight, and all of those algorithms and encryption methods would be validated. That would make solving the Riemann Hypothesis one of the greatest mathematical breakthroughs in history.

Recent findings suggest that “It is certainly an exciting time,” Paul Milewski, head of the department of mathematics at Penn State, said in an email to CNET. “The Riemann Hypothesis (or any big theorem) is often not the ‘goal’ of mathematics. They are set up as grand challenges that require the development of latest tools, new results along the way and new understanding. It is the ‘voyage’ and not the destination that matters the most.”.

As such, the mathematics community wasted no time testing the proof to see whether it was true. Two groups — Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative — independently verified the proof, with many other researchers running their own tests and coming to the same conclusion.

“We have full confidence that Alpöge’s proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him on the achievement,” the two groups said in a joint statement on Saturday.

This is certainly an exciting discovery, but it’s not without its obstacles. Alpöge’s proof was a staggering 250,000 pages of some of the most complex math ever written by a human or a machine. Alpöge provided 17 million lines of Lean code, a programming language specifically made for writing and checking proofs, and that’s how researchers were able to check the work and show it to be true.

The problem is that the average novel is about 300 pages, and that means that Alpöge’s AI-assisted proof is approximately 833 novels’ worth of complex math. For reference, the longest work ever produced is World-2023, which holds the Guinness World Record at 100,100 pages. That book is 19 feet tall, and Alpöge’s proof is two and a half times longer.

It has been revealed that despite the logic being verified as true through Lean code, Alpöge still has a major problem. So far, none of the mathematicians or researchers who have attempted to read it have been able to understand what it claims.

Sources indicate that “I do not understand, and I suspect no human completely understands,” Jon Keating, professor of mathematical physics at the University of Oxford, said in a Numberphile YouTube video. “When I look at that, I’m completely in awe and in wonderment.”.

It has been revealed that for the problem to be fully solved, the proof has to be read, analyzed and simplified so that it can be translated into readable mathematics, which Alpöge says in his announcement that he’s in the process of doing. All of this has to be done so that Alpöge can publish it in a peer-reviewed journal in such a way that his peers can actually read it. It is only after the mathematics community scrutinizes and accepts Alpöge’s proof that it is considered fully solved.

Aside from being nigh unreadable to humans, Alpöge has otherwise avoided the kinds of drama that other AI-assisted discoveries have faced in 2026.

OpenAI had to backtrack on its proof of the Navier-Stokes problem, which is another Millennium Problem, after the manufacturer couldn’t rule out that the AI models it used had access to data from other researchers. Somewhat ironically, one of those mathematicians whose work OpenAI may have  — knowingly or unknowingly — borrowed from was Levent Alpöge, as he and others were pretty close to solving the problem on their own.

Similarly, Claude was credited with finding a latest novel enzyme that humans had never seen before. The problem is that computational biologist Mario Rodríguez Mestre had seen this enzyme before and was using Claude to study it further, so it’s uncertain if Claude actually found it independently or used data from Mestre’s research to find it.

The heavy assistance from AI has been met with mostly positive reactions, with most researchers agreeing that the AI usage is justified provided that the proof is proven to be true through peer review. Since no one was particularly close to solving the Riemann Hypothesis, there haven’t been any accusations of Alpöge or Claude stealing work like those prior examples. By and large, most mathematicians are excited about the discovery.

According to recent reports, “Even before this, we have seen the power of AI, and this highlights that AI trained on hundreds of years of human mathematics can perform amazing tasks,” noted Penn State’s Milewski. “I would add that AI didn’t come up with the Riemann Hypothesis, nor did most of the work to prove it, and AI probably doesn’t ‘know’ why it was invented or why it’s important.”.

CNET spoke with a few professors about this, and they all echoed Milewski’s sentiment, stating that AI was trained with centuries of human mathematical achievement, so a win for AI is a win for humans too. Jeffrey Lagarias, a professor of mathematics at the University of Michigan, told CNET that “I don’t think this particular proof would have been found without AI.”.

Prasad Tetali, head of the department of mathematical sciences at Carnegie Mellon University, noted: “It is easy to overestimate the role of AI, and underappreciate decades of human mathematician work that went into it. The AI here is really standing tall and wide on the shoulders of generations of human giants.”.

According to recent reports, on the AI side of things, influencers are attempting to use the news to hype up the capabilities of AI. Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang stated in a post on X that solving the Riemann Hypothesis was a sign that AI superintelligence was close at hand and that humanity should be terrified of the “alien mind that we don’t understand.”.

AI researcher Eliezer Yudkowsky likened the whole thing to a company making enriched uranium that’ll one day result in the end of the human species.

Industry observers note that these warnings are hard to take seriously when one considers that Anthropic tried to make Claude solve the Riemann Hypothesis by itself back in August. Claude came up with some cool ideas but ultimately failed to solve the problem alone. For the time being, AI still needs a great deal of human guidance to make these massive discoveries, so the doom-and-gloom proselytizing comes off as a little premature.

Sources indicate that to make things even more interesting, a competing Riemann Hypothesis proof was submitted by Alessandro Masullo just a few hours after Alpöge released his. This competing proof is 940 pages long, which is significantly shorter than Alpöge’s proof, and it was an all-human effort with no AI assistance. The proof is months in the making, with Masullo working with mathematician Brian Conrad to bring it up to spec before it hits peer review. When Alpöge posted his proof, Masullo and others thought it wise to submit theirs as well.

This started a “dueling proofs” storyline over the weekend, but it was short-lived. Shortly after Masullo’s proof was posted, multiple people found the types of flaws and omissions that often disprove Riemann Hypothesis proofs. Those issues are in the process of being corrected, and the proof is officially in mid-revision status.

Masullo kept the original proof posted (PDF) in its unedited form, but acknowledges that the proof was rushed to publication so that it could compete with Alpöge and Claude.

Sources indicate that “The PDF below was posted on Nov. 20 on Ravi Vakil’s blog,” Masullo wrote on a Google site. “It was never meant to be shared publicly at this stage, and it has been posted in this draft form in response to current circumstances.”.

It’s entirely possible that future revisions of Masullo’s work may solve the problems in the early draft and create a fully human proof of the Riemann Hypothesis without AI, but that isn’t happening anytime soon.

This is a lot of information about finding the Riemann Hypothesis, so it’s probably a good idea to briefly explain what it even is. In the 1730s, famous mathematician Leonhard Euler came up with a zeta function as a way to solve the Basel Problem, another mathematical curiosity about the exact sum of the reciprocals of squares. Euler was successful in this endeavor, and the zeta function became a part of mathematics.

Industry observers note that bernhard Riemann picked up where Euler left off and expanded the zeta function to use complex numbers — real numbers mixed with imaginary numbers — using a process called analytic continuation. Riemann used this expanded function to express how many prime numbers there were under a specific number and how tightly those prime numbers were packed together.

This is easy enough to do in your head with small numbers, like figuring out there are four prime numbers under 10, but when the biggest prime number is 41,024,320 digits long, having a function to do it for you is a lot more helpful.

The mechanics of Riemann’s expanded zeta function are quite complicated, and the math-focused YouTube channel Numberphile has an excellent explainer from a professional mathematician (with pictures) if you want to learn more.

The hypothesis concerns the solutions the function yields. Riemann’s version of the zeta function demonstrated that if you plugged in an even negative number, like -2, -4 or -672, the function would always spit out a zero. These are referred to as trivial zeroes, and Riemann proved that this was always true in his original paper.

Industry observers note that the Riemann Hypothesis is the conjecture that all the other numbers that would also make a zero — referred to as non-trivial zeroes — follow a very specific formula, which is “½ + it”, where “i” is an imaginary number and “t” is any real number, positive or negative. In short, Riemann believed that there was no other way to generate a zero with his zeta function other than even negative numbers (trivial zeroes) and numbers that followed the “½+it” formula (non-trivial zeroes). Riemann provided some examples of the hypothesis being right but never wrote a full proof of it.

It’s worth noting that not every number that follows the “½+it” formula produces a zero, but that all the numbers that produce a zero will use that formula. It’s kind of the same as saying that all squares are rectangles but not all rectangles are squares.

In a recent development, in the 167 years since the hypothesis was first published, mathematicians have found 12 trillion non-trivial zeroes, and every single one of them fits the above rules. Trillions of other numbers that don’t follow those rules have been tested to find a counterexample, since even one counterexample disproves the hypothesis immediately. Those efforts have produced no counterexamples at all.

This isn’t conclusive proof, but it’s such an overwhelming amount of evidence that mathematicians began assuming that the hypothesis was true, even if no one could prove it. Alpöge’s AI-assisted proof is the first to show in any context that the hypothesis is always true, which, according to Tetali, has implications in prime number understanding, number theory and other branches of mathematics.

Recent findings suggest that “The big job on the math side is to find a human-understandable proof,” Lagarias noted. “I would say this is certainly going to happen; there will be such understanding. Already there are several AI digests of the proof breaking it into its component pieces. I have seen one [that’s] 11 pages, 164 pages, 273 pages. There are great ideas to extract from them.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

So too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this fresh take on the OS is the epitome of that.

The distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with new ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”.

Industry observers note that the developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

The Pond UI consists of the following:.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend.

Sources indicate that if you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:.

It has been revealed that pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind.

At the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a new workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

Pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

Another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:.

Once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

In a recent development, as I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One issue that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI patch system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:.

I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an update component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux.

In a recent development, it would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

You should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my new favorite free productivity suite.

Industry observers note that pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

  • Unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the newly introduced MacBook Neo. If you’re deciding between the MacBook Neo and the MacBook Air this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

The MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop ever, starting at $699 (currently on sale for $599). It features a solid aluminum design that comes in a range of fun colors, including Silver, Blush, Citrus, and Indigo.

Unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip. It uses the A18 Pro chip originally introduced with the iPhone 16 Pro, featuring a 6-core CPU and 5-core GPU.

Recent findings suggest that the MacBook Neo comes with 8GB of unified memory, with no additional RAM configuration options available. It starts with 256GB of storage, with a 512GB configuration available for an additional $100. That $100 upgrade also gets you Touch ID, which is not included in the base model.

It has been revealed that there are some other trade-offs compared to the MacBook Air. The MacBook Neo lacks a backlit keyboard, MagSafe charging, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also has more limited USB-C connectivity and supports just one external display.

According to recent reports, still, the MacBook Neo offers an impressive feature set. It has a 13-inch display, up to 16 hours of battery life, a 1080p FaceTime camera, and the full macOS experience.

Industry observers note that the MacBook Air, meanwhile, was updated earlier this year with Apple’s M5 chip. It starts at $1,299, making it $600 more expensive than the entry-level MacBook Air. The MacBook Air is currently on sale with a starting price of $999.

For that $600 upgrade, the MacBook Air offers several key advantages over the MacBook Air. The M5 chip has a 10-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU, enabling better sustained performance than the MacBook Neo.

The MacBook Air also starts with 16GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage, both double the entry-level MacBook Neo. You can configure it with up to 32GB of memory and 4TB of storage, while the MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB of memory and 512GB of storage.

Apple rates the MacBook Air for up to 18 hours of video streaming and 15 hours of wireless web browsing, compared to 16 hours and 11 hours, respectively, for the MacBook Neo.

As I wrote in my review earlier this year, I think the MacBook Neo is a great Mac, full stop … not just because of the great price. It can handle the vast majority of things most people will throw at it. This includes web browsing, basic photo and video editing, research, and much more.

Recent findings suggest that the M5 MacBook Air, meanwhile, offers more power and more configuration options. This makes it a great option for people who need more storage, RAM, and power than the MacBook Neo can offer.

It has been revealed that one of my favorite things about the MacBook Air is that it’s available in two screen sizes. The 15-inch MacBook Air is one of my favorite Apple laptops with a combination of the ultra-thin and light design and the larger screen. I think a lot of people forget it exists, but it’s an excellent choice.

To recap, I think the MacBook Neo is a great choice for everyday tasks like web browsing, email, writing, and streaming. The MacBook Air is a better fit for more demanding workflows, including photo and video editing, coding, working with large spreadsheets, and heavy multitasking.

It has been revealed that beyond performance, the MacBook Air offers a handful of niceties that you won’t find on the MacBook Neo. These include a backlit keyboard, a larger display with True Tone, MagSafe charging, a better webcam and speakers, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also includes Touch ID on every configuration, longer battery life, and support for two external displays.

It has been revealed that if it’s in the budget, I think the MacBook Air is an excellent choice for all Mac shoppers. It’s plenty powerful, thin and light, and is highly configurable compared to the MacBook Neo.
