#131191. I Tried Using Meta Muse and ChatGPT Dots to Save on Groceries. They’re Not Quite There Yet

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1164 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

I Tried Using Meta Muse and ChatGPT Dots to Save on Groceries. They’re Not Quite There Yet

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1164 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • High grocery prices have been in the news for years now.
  • So before you drop a fortune on gas and drive out to the grocery store to spend even more on sustenance in your prep for hosting or bringing dishes to your holiday celebrations, you might consider using an AI agent to find you the best deal possible.
  • Although, in my experience, it’s not as simple as the AI marketing makes it sound.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

High grocery prices have been in the news for years now. The cost of eggs, how much you’re paying for a bowl of cereal and whether or not meat is back on the menu are the recurring subjects of nationwide headlines.

So before you drop a fortune on gas and drive out to the grocery store to spend even more on sustenance in your prep for hosting or bringing dishes to your holiday celebrations, you might consider using an AI agent to find you the best deal possible.

Although, in my experience, it’s not as simple as the AI marketing makes it sound. Here’s what happened when I tried to use AI agents to find the lowest possible prices on groceries.

AI agents such as Meta Muse and ChatGPT’s Dots can only crawl so many sites and online fliers for prices. Some stores and e-commerce sites have blocked AI agents from accessing their URLs. The first step in finding cheaper groceries with AI agents is to check which sites and stores they can access for price comparisons.

Where both agents missed a step was in the limitations they put on their searches, at first only looking at the retailers I had shown via my receipts and a few other big-name grocery stores.

I clarified in the chats and in a 20-minute voice conversation with Muse and a 14-minute voice conversation with Dots that they should expand their horizons and look at discount online retailers like Martie.com, and check what they could around advertised pricing and offerings at local farmers’ markets.

Muse stuck to the basics like Ralphs, Target and Walmart, and then expanded to Sprouts, Vons and Martie.com when prompted.

After further nudging, Muse also reviewed user-reported pricing from Costco (I don’t have a membership), gave me vague information about Grocery Outlet, suggested Misfits Market/Imperfect Foods, ruled out Amazon Fresh and gave me some sample pricing from a local butcher for meats.

Muse also checked some local bakery prices after I mentioned I’d like to find alternatives to sweet treats at a more affordable price.

Dots checked all the usual places that Meta Muse checked with a few extras thrown in — Smart & Final for produce, meat and some packaged products, and Super King’s monthly ad.

Neither of the tools checked Trader Joe’s. Muse said that the grocery chain doesn’t show prices of its products online, despite me finding that the Trader Joe’s website demonstrates prices of its products online. Both Dots and Muse admitted to only checking the local store’s pages when asked.

According to recent reports, you could spend some time making a list from scratch of all the groceries you might need every two weeks and give that list to the AI agent for its search. You could also skip all that and take some pics of your most recent grocery receipts and online payments and have the AI agent build the list itself.

I had some receipts saved, and the AI agents I used for this test were able to put together an accurate grocery list from them. I also provided emails showing receipts from online orders of household items and groceries for the past month to build my orders.

Recent findings suggest that muse took my receipts and concluded that, surprise, surprise, shopping at Gelson’s was not as cost-effective as shopping at Walmart. It spat out a lot of specific information about comparisons on some of the items in my list, but completely ignored others.

Dots looked over my receipts and recommended I try shopping at Super King for most fresh meat, produce and a few grains, and keep Walmart as my main option for packaged products like pasta sauce.

Both tools tackled this task in a way I was not expecting — as a narrative exploration of my overall grocery spending, with generalized suggestions supported by specific examples of spot pricing.

It was kind of like they’ve been optimized to write essays about grocery shopping as a school assignment, and not to be agentic personal assistants for real-world work.

Maybe it was the way I phrased the task, but I was hoping to get an actual shopping list with price comparisons for each item, or at least equivalent items, and a guide on where and how to procure mentioned items.

Neither AI agent provided this autonomously and had to be directly prompted to provide grocery lists in response to a very specific request.

AI agents are supposed to be pros at anticipating the needs of their human bosses. I was keen to see how the always-on AI agents would handle managing the recurring needs of a small household and if they might make any autonomous suggestions meant to save me money in ways I hadn’t anticipated.

At no point did Muse seem to be actually thinking outside the strict parameters of the review of the items on the receipts I sent. This felt more like a conversation about what I’d previously purchased with a side serving of attempts to get me to connect Instacart to the tool.

It was also the most confusing grocery shopping experience I have ever had. That might be on me, but I would assume the agent might ask some questions, like how often I usually shop, what my monthly budget for groceries is, and how many people and animals live in the house. Muse didn’t ask any of those things and had to be prompted consistently.

Recent findings suggest that muse sent me the final grocery list as a raw Markdown file, which was hilarious. I got a .pdf version after explicitly asking for one.

My original total with one in-person shop and one online order was about $180. Muse’s total with three in-person shops and one online order came in at around $153.

Dots was slightly better suited to this task after some prodding, and gave me some options for building prep meals with low-effort, high-protein recipes based on how I usually shop.

Dots’ final grocery list included everything I asked for, but still missed some key items, like solid substitutes for pricey prepped foods. Dot’s final total with two in-person shopping trips and a whole lot of missing items came out to around $85.

This test reinforced my findings about how agentic AI tools tackle domestic or traditionally invisible labor tasks. In my limited use cases so far, they are about as useful as a loose dog turd tumbling around in a clothes dryer.

If you’re not looking to book a flight and hotel for a business conference in Philadelphia or put your Sweetgreen order on autopilot, the AI agents exhibit a startling lack of curiosity and autonomous thinking.

Industry observers note that there’s still a large gap in common sense on the part of agentic AI for those of us hoping these tools will make our everyday lives outside of a 9-to-5 easier, more affordable or less hectic. I hope that changes as they learn.

  • Recent findings suggest that what's more, TechInsights predicts that the industry's revenue will soar to $2.6 trillion next year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Harsh Chauhan – Nov 26, 2026 at 10:32AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Lam Research ›.

Though semiconductor stocks have taken a beating lately, a closer look at the financial performance of companies in this sector clearly indicates that the sell-off isn't justified.

Recent findings suggest that the semiconductor industry's revenue has been growing at an impressive pace, driven by rising demand for chips used in artificial intelligence (AI) applications, especially in data centers. This explains why the semiconductor industry's revenue in 2026 is anticipated to increase by 111% to $1.8 trillion, according to semiconductor intelligence provider TechInsights.

Recent findings suggest that what's more, TechInsights predicts that the industry's revenue will soar to $2.6 trillion next year. That's why now is a good time to take a closer look at a top semiconductor stock while it trades at an attractive valuation -- Lam Research (LRCX -5.68%) -- before it steps on the gas next year.

According to recent reports, techInsights estimates that the memory market's revenue could hit $1.6 trillion next year, accounting for 61% of the overall semiconductor market. The firm adds that the memory market could clock higher revenue next year if there are no supply constraints.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Not surprisingly, memory manufacturers are ramping up capital expenditures. Micron Technology, for instance, is estimating $25 billion in capex for the first half of fiscal 2027, followed by higher spending in the second half. Micron spent $27.4 billion on capex in fiscal 2026, suggesting its spending could double this year.

Recent findings suggest that given that memory supply conditions are expected to tighten in 2027 and 2028, according to Micron, and other memory manufacturers expect the shortage to last until 2030, I won't be surprised to see memory capex jump higher in the coming years. This is great news for Lam Research, a semiconductor equipment firm that's benefiting from the memory shortage.

Lam Research's revenue in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 shot up by 54% from the year-ago period. The company reported non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) of $2.20, up 75% from the year-ago period. Investors should note that Lam Research gets 46% of its revenue from sales of memory manufacturing equipment, which explains the impressive growth in revenue and earnings. Specifically, Lam's revenue from sales of memory equipment increased by 120% year over year in the previous quarter.

Sources indicate that even better, Lam's growth is poised to accelerate in the current quarter. The company's $8.6 billion revenue estimate for the current quarter implies a 61% increase over the year-ago period. The adjusted EPS estimate of $2.33 would be an 83% improvement from the same quarter last year. As investments in memory manufacturing equipment increase in 2027 and beyond, Lam should be able to sustain its solid growth rate.

Analysts are forecasting a 66% increase in its EPS in the current fiscal year (which ends in June next year). They are expecting healthy double-digit growth over the next two fiscal years as well, though don't be surprised to see it outperform those expectations due to the tight memory supply, which will encourage manufacturers to invest in more capital equipment.

LRCX EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts.

Sources indicate that in fact, Lam estimates that spending on wafer and fabrication equipment (WFE) could increase from the mid-$150 billion range this year to more than $200 billion in 2027. That implies a potential increase of almost 30%.

Industry observers note that lam management noted on the recent earnings call that it has been gaining market share in the WFE space and sees opportunities for further share gains. So, there is a strong likelihood that Lam's growth will outpace analysts' expectations in 2027 and beyond.

Sources indicate that lam Research stock has lost 53% of its value since the beginning of July. The stock trades at just 19 times forward earnings, only a slight premium to the S&P 500 index's forward earnings multiple of 18.

We have already seen that Lam's EPS is on track to increase by 66% this year, well above the 34% growth that S&P 500 companies are expected to deliver. Analysts expect Lam to outperform the S&P 500's earnings growth next year as well. So, it is easy to see why this semiconductor stock is expected to soar by 89% over the coming year, based on the 12-month median price target of $350, according to CNN.

All this indicates that Lam Research is an AI stock worth buying hand over fist following its recent pullback, as it could step on the gas in 2027 amid strong semiconductor sales.

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (906 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Claude can ship code for you now – how to try it (if you dare)

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (906 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it.
  • According to recent reports, with Claude Ship, revealed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic stated.
  • Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A new feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

According to recent reports, with Claude Ship, revealed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic stated. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

“Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic said. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

Industry observers note that the fresh feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise intends. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic said, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

Recent findings suggest that as a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic mentioned.

Sources indicate that “It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic remarked it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic said in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz said the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

According to recent reports, also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

According to recent reports, “But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he remarked. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

Ultimately, Gewirtz remarked he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the company and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he remarked.

According to recent reports, developer platforms overall are adapting to the latest state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

It has been revealed that individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “people won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

Still, that depends on the number of PRs customers are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the new PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

It has been revealed that anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

Sources indicate that you would have paid $900 for this Legion Go S configuration at launch, and as much as $1,608 after that as gaming component costs rise. At $850, you’ll be paying $50 less than the launch price.

If the Legion Go S isn’t the right handheld for you, you can pick from a few alternatives from CNET’s list of the best handheld gaming consoles.

Industry observers note that the Nintendo Switch 2 is our pick for the best overall gaming handheld, with a CNET score of 8.5 out of 10. The Switch 2 has a slim design with a large 1080p display, and the controllers attach magnetically. We got less battery life from the Switch 2 than from the original Switch in our testing. Nintendo only lets you play games bought on game cards or through the eShop, so you won’t be able to bring your Steam library to the Switch 2.

Valve’s Steam Deck OLED uses the same SteamOS software as the Legion Go S. The Steam Deck OLED has an HDR OLED display, and we liked the controls and the improved haptics in our testing. Valve is selling the Steam Deck OLED for $789, which is $61 less than the Legion Go S. The Steam Deck OLED has a smaller screen than the Legion Go S, though, so you’ll have to decide if the $61 saving makes up for the difference in size.

According to recent reports, the ROG Xbox Ally X runs Windows, so you can install games from multiple game stores without any workarounds. The grips are larger than the ones on most handhelds, which can make the ROG Xbox Ally X more comfortable to hold. We found the performance to be excellent in lighter games, but Windows can sometimes slow the handheld down. At $1,000 at Best Buy, the ROG Xbox Ally X is $150 more expensive than the Legion Go S.

It depends on the handheld. Lenovo has cut the Legion Go S with SteamOS to $850, from $1,608, for Black Friday. But we haven’t found Black Friday discounts on the Nintendo Switch 2, the Steam Deck OLED or the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X yet. You’ll find more discounts in other categories right now, including Best Buy’s Black Friday OLED TV deals and our Black Friday headphone deals.

You likely won’t gain much by waiting. Lenovo has labeled the $850 price a doorbuster, and we don’t know how long the stock will last. Best Buy’s Black Friday sale recently had the same model for $901, which is $51 more than Lenovo’s price. Lenovo is also offering a price match guarantee and extended returns through Jan. 27, in case you find a lower price during Amazon’s Black Friday sale or Walmart’s Black Friday sale.

Sources indicate that CNET Senior Editor Lori Grunin prefers the Legion Go S with SteamOS, which has a larger display and a different control layout. The Steam Deck OLED is still our pick for the best PC handheld on our list of the best handheld gaming consoles, and it’s the one I would buy myself. The Steam Deck OLED has an HDR OLED display, while the Legion Go S has an LCD screen. The Legion Go S and the Steam Deck OLED both use SteamOS, so you should be able to play most of the same Steam games on either handheld.

    #131169. The FCC Approved a Million SpaceX Satellites for Data Centers in Space

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (597 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    The FCC Approved a Million SpaceX Satellites for Data Centers in Space

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (597 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space.
    • Industry observers note that spaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind.
    • Industry observers note that “It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space.

    Industry observers note that spaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind. The FCC’s approval requires that SpaceX launch its first data center satellite by 2030 and meet the 1 million mark by 2040.

    Industry observers note that “It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing. Is this actually safe?’” Jonathan McDowell, an astrophysicist who tracks satellite launches, told CNET. “It’s a blank check. Launch as many satellites as you can, and we’ll just see what happens. I think this is a mistake on the FCC’s part.”.

    Orbital data centers have long been a goal of SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, becoming a pivotal part of his pitch to investors ahead of the organization’s IPO in June.

    “You’re power-constrained on Earth. Space has the advantage that it’s always sunny,” Musk stated in March.

    In a recent development, on its web page for Starmind, SpaceX touts its high-efficiency solar arrays on the planned satellites and the cooling benefits of space. It claims that high-speed laser links will beam the AI results back to Earth through Starlink’s constellation.

    Space experts I’ve talked to this year about Starmind have been skeptical. The technical challenges alone are dizzying; the scale of SpaceX’s ambitions is hard to swallow.

    It’s taken seven years for Starlink to grow its constellation to 11,195 satellites, and that was already an unprecedented feat. Is it possible to get to 1 million satellites in 14 years?

    Sources indicate that “We do not have the launch capacity for any of this,” Ian Christensen, senior director at the Secure World Foundation, told me in a previous interview. “Not even within SpaceX to do their own constellation, let alone the other constellations planned.”.

    SpaceX has increasingly prioritized launching its own satellites instead of letting commercial customers hitch a ride on their rockets. Starlink’s share of SpaceX missions has gone from 54% of its Falcon 9 rocket’s missions in 2020 to about 79% in 2026, according to a Reuters analysis. One analysis estimates that SpaceX would have to launch 5,000 Starship rockets a year to meet its goal — a staggering increase from 330 rockets that launched last year in total.

    Scientists have already been ringing alarm bells about overcrowded orbits as they exist now. The more satellites in space, the more difficult it is for operators to maneuver around each other. A single crash could turn into decades of orbital debris, which could cause a chain reaction that eventually makes space inoperable for everyone. And burning up all those satellites in the atmosphere when they reach the end of their lives has already started to leave ozone-depleting aluminum particles behind. A paper published this week in Earth and Space Chemistry estimated that SpaceX’s data center strategy would multiply pollutants in the upper atmosphere by more than 150 times compared to last year.

    “There are scientific papers out there raising challenges,” McDowell said. “Yes, they’re unproven, but if I say, ‘Yeah, we’re not sure if this is going to destroy the atmosphere and kill us all, but it might,’ is the right reaction to go, ‘Well, you haven’t proven it, so we’re just going to ignore it’?”.

    The FCC’s approval came despite objections from Amazon, the environmental nonprofit Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility and the American Astronomical Society.

    A representative for SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google has added Wallet integration to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, letting you learn about your spending habits, blueprint a budget, maximize credit card rewards, and more with a simple Search.

    Starting today, Google confirmed, Personal Intelligence for Search is expanding to more apps, including Wallet and Drive. Google can’t move or manage any money, but it can give you tailored, personalized search results about your finances, like showing where you spend the most, identifying recurring subscriptions you might not be aware of, and suggesting which credit card might be best to use for travel. All you have to do is ask in a search.

    Also: I tried Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – and it knew exactly where I wanted to go.

    This feature comes just over a week after Google introduced Personal Intelligence to Wallet.

    Once your Wallet is connected, it takes a few minutes to fully sync. Once it’s finished, you can ask questions through AI mode in Search.

    I decided to give it a try for myself, starting off with a simple query: “Based on my spending, what’s a quick way I can save money?” I could have told you one of the primary culprits, but Google happily responded with what I already knew: far too much of my money goes to fast food and coffee.

    “You frequently grab quick-service meals,” the response said, pointing out several fast food places that I do indeed frequent, “and specialty coffees throughout the week.” If I just cut that down to two meals and two coffees a week, Gemini explained, I’d save about $30 a week, or $1,500 a year.

    Also: This powerful Gemini setting made my AI results way more personal and accurate.

    Recent findings suggest that when I asked it to find recurring subscriptions, Gemini noted that I had several monthly charges. What I didn’t ask for, but it did, was to break down those subscriptions into an easy-to-see chart, complete with the name, price, category, the card it’s being charged to, and the timeframe it usually comes out. Gemini even offered a few free alternatives to services I was paying for.

    Since Gemini also knows what cards are linked to your Wallet, it’s able to offer advice there, too. I’m planning a trip to Newly introduced York City, so I asked which cards might be best to use for the hotels and airfare. Gemini was able to analyze my card benefits, considering things like rewards and built-in travel insurance, and make a recommendation.

    Industry observers note that also: Slow Android phone? How to speed it back up in 4 easy steps.

    While Gemini Personal Intelligence can access your Gmail to learn more about your spending, it can’t access your bank account. The only information it knows about your finances and spending comes from receipts in your inbox or from your Wallet transaction history. I do use Wallet often (mostly when ordering through online apps), but it’s not quite my go-to option when I’m in a store. Given how useful this feature can be, though, I might just start using Wallet more to give it more information to work with.

    S&P 500 Sell-Off: Here's Why I'm Not Panicking -- and What I'm Doing Instead

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, monday was a great example of why investors shouldn't panic sell during a correction or significant market downturn.
    • 20, the Nasdaq had been in near bear market territory, down 18% from its all-time high of 27,599 on Oct.
    • If you did sell shares in a Nasdaq or tech-focused ETF, or a stock like Nvidia, which gained some 30% on the day alone after CEO Jensen Huang was rehired, you would have lost out on a huge return.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Dave Kovaleski – Nov 26, 2026 at 10:45AM EST.

    In a recent development, monday was a great example of why investors shouldn't panic sell during a correction or significant market downturn. On Nov. 23, the S&P 500 jumped nearly 5%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 3% and the Nasdaq Composite had one of its best days ever, rising 1,471 points, or 6.5%.

    In a recent development, as of Nov. 20, the Nasdaq had been in near bear market territory, down 18% from its all-time high of 27,599 on Oct. 6. But on Nov. 23, with its nearly 1,500-point gain, it surged to 24,089. It is still down 12% from Oct. 6, and there may be volatile days ahead, but days like Monday are one reason you don't want to panic sell during a downturn.

    If you did sell shares in a Nasdaq or tech-focused ETF, or a stock like Nvidia, which gained some 30% on the day alone after CEO Jensen Huang was rehired, you would have lost out on a huge return.

    And it's just not a one-off type scenario that won't ever happen again. There are stats to show how much it can negatively impact your portfolio when you miss the market's best days during the correction of a bear market.

    Image source: OpenAI (AI-generated illustration).

    Earlier this year, the Hartford Funds released a report that examined this very subject. It found that from 1950 through 2025, 76% of the market's best days were either during a bear market or within the first two months of a bull market. Of that, 48% came during a bear market. We're not yet in a bear market, but that could certainly change in the months ahead.

    According to recent reports, the Hartford report also compiled some numbers on how missing out on the best days would affect a long-term portfolio. It revealed that $10,000 invested in the S&P 500 in 1996 would grow to $192,167 after 30 years, through 2025, based on the average annual total returns of the S&P 500.

    If you missed the market's 10 best days, that would bring it down to $85,490. If you missed the best 20 days, the total would be $49,551. If you missed the market's best 30 days, you'd have $31,123 -- 84% less than if you stayed fully invested all 30 years.

    Sources indicate that fidelity did a similar study in August, putting a slightly finer point on it. It looks at the impact of missing the market's best days since 1988. A $10,000 investment in the S&P 500 from Jan. 1, 1988 to Dec. 31, 2025 would generate $616,013. Missing just the five best days would result in 38% less in your portfolio, about $380,479.

    There are a few things to understand that should help guide you through bear markets and rough patches.

    Recent findings suggest that one, understand that bear markets do not last as long as bull markets, nor do they have a bigger net effect on your portfolio.     • According to recent reports, if you, like me, are the type of person who makes a lot of to-do lists and can’t breathe a sigh of relief until you check items off them, I have some bad news.
    • Recent findings suggest that we’ve seen no announcement or acknowledgment in the app itself that To Do, which debuted in 2017, would be retired.
    • For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, if you, like me, are the type of person who makes a lot of to-do lists and can’t breathe a sigh of relief until you check items off them, I have some bad news. One of the best free options for organizing your work and home life is reaching the end of its life. Microsoft looks to retire its To Do app at the end of June 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that we’ve seen no announcement or acknowledgment in the app itself that To Do, which debuted in 2017, would be retired. But several Microsoft-watching websites this week spotted a blog post from the organization recommending users switch to its Planner app.

    Microsoft To Do is retiring. For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.

    According to recent reports, microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027. This includes To Do on the web, Windows, Mac, iOS, and Android, for both work or school accounts and personal Microsoft accounts.

    In a recent development, the underlying To Do service, APIs, and related synchronization support will retire on separate, later timelines. We’ll communicate those dates and any required preparation separately.

    Sources indicate that but there’s a big catch for Microsoft customers who are on 365 Personal or 365 Family aims: Planner will not be available to them. That means Microsoft is telling To Do users on those accounts to find a comparable app elsewhere if they’re not on a business account that includes Planner.

    The change was also mentioned in a separate Microsoft post about unified tasks and prepares for Copilot and Microsoft 365 from Microsoft product manager Ashna Patel.

    In a statement provided to CNET, Howard Crow, director of product, agents and AI at Microsoft, mentioned the change consolidates task management across Microsoft 365. “We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare,” Crow said.

    Crow stated the company will share more information about the transition in the coming months.

    Industry observers note that while the end of June 2027 may sound like a very long time from now, the path Microsoft has offered for To Do users is not a great one if you want to take action now. There’s no built-in export feature in the app, though in the blog post, Microsoft promises, “Microsoft will provide a way to export your To Do data before the apps retire. We’ll update this article with instructions, supported data, requirements, and limitations when those details are finalized.”.

    In a recent development, already, there are some pretty severe limitations even for those on Microsoft aims that support Planner: Existing To Do list items won’t work after that June deadline. “After that date, you will no longer be able to view or manage them in Planner,” the post said.

    In the meantime, you can shop around for alternate apps, some free, including Google Keep, ToDoist and Notion.

    To Do consumers, myself included, are not happy. As Windows Latest reported, comments in response to Microsoft’s decision included, “Do you actually hate your users?”.

    Industry observers note that if this were simply a case of Microsoft creating software people didn’t like and then abandoning it, that would be one thing. But the To Do retirement is especially painful for those of us who were forced to move to Microsoft’s app a few years after it purchased Wunderlist.

    Wunderlist was a German app that debuted in 2011 and rapidly became popular for its slick interface, easy-to-update task lists and its availability across web, desktop and mobile platforms. Microsoft absorbed some of Wunderlist into To Do and killed the original app in 2020 without ever offering all of the features that made Wunderlist great.

    As someone who used Wunderlist for years and has been using To Do, I can tell you that while To Do has been essential in my work and personal life, it never became as intuitive to use as Wunderlist. It never handled predictive task creation as well as Wunderlist did (such as understanding as you typed the date of a task or if it was repeating). It lacked features for sharing lists or collaborating on them, and simply didn’t look as stylish. As far as aesthetics, the best thing Microsoft did with To Do was add a Dark Mode.

    Sources indicate that wunderlist was a joy to use. To Do always felt like the knockoff diet version of it and never quite as good.

    After several years, I simply gave up on the idea that Microsoft would improve the app or add any upcoming features, but kept using it out of necessity given the lack of a built-in export option.

    Sources indicate that the death announcement is not surprising. Just sad.

    RIP To Do, but really RIP to the last remnants of Wunderlist.

    • According to recent reports, generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations.
    • Gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found.
    • Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations. That’s according to a survey from talent services firm Seramount, which found that Gen Z was the most AI-averse among the generations surveyed about using the technology in their jobs.

    Gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found. Only 18% of Gen Z reported an interest in strengthening their AI skills, compared to 36% of Millennials, 46% of Gen Xers, and 43% of Boomers. Gen Z is also using AI less than other generations, by nine percentage points.

    Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.

    “Employers cannot assume their youngest employees will embrace AI on their own,” noted Diana Forster, senior director of research at Seramount.

    The survey polled responses from over 1,800 US white-collar workers at companies with at least 500 employees.

    Around half of Gen Z report weekly AI use (not specific to work), according to a survey from Walton Family Foundation, GSV Ventures and Gallup, but the generation’s skepticism has mounted over the past few years. Even members of Gen Z who use AI daily have less positive views on the technology. In the same study, 42% of Gen Z reported feeling anxious about AI in 2026, a 1% increase from 2025. Last year, 36% of Gen Z respondents reported excitement about AI. In 2026, that percentage dropped to 22%.

    Also: These companies are actually upskilling their workers for AI – here’s how they do it.

    Industry observers note that it’s no surprise Gen Z is skeptical about adopting a technology that could be undermining their own career development. The labor market has been particularly harsh to this group of workers, as entry-level job postings have fallen in recent years, and many fear that AI will only exacerbate unemployment. Around 8% of those ages 22 to 24 were unemployed in September, compared to 3% of workers ages 25 to 54, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

    But with many workplaces still adopting AI, senior employees are trying to prepare Gen Z by getting them on board at work.

    “We need to show young workers how AI can strengthen their work, provide clear guidelines and training, and give them opportunities to practice using it and build the skills they’ll need as leaders,” Forster mentioned.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    We Shot a Ship Into an Asteroid to See if It Would Move. See the First Images of the Impact

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (936 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that five years ago, NASA launched its DART spacecraft with the express intent of ramming it into Dimorphos, an asteroid orbiting the larger Didymos asteroid, to see if its trajectory could be changed.
    • The ESA livestreamed the presentation on Tuesday to the delight of cosmic rubberneckers everywhere.
    • It has been revealed that at the time of the mission, the only instruments that could see the impact and the massive cloud of debris flying off Dimorphos were the Hubble Space Telescope and multiple telescopes on Earth.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that five years ago, NASA launched its DART spacecraft with the express intent of ramming it into Dimorphos, an asteroid orbiting the larger Didymos asteroid, to see if its trajectory could be changed. The mission was a success, making Dimorphos the first celestial object whose orbit was moved by humans. And now, the European Space Agency has published images showing the damage the mission caused to the asteroid.

    The ESA livestreamed the presentation on Tuesday to the delight of cosmic rubberneckers everywhere. The images shown during the livestream were captured by the ESA’s Hera, which was introduced in October 2024 and spent two years in deep space with its two CubeSats to measure, map, probe and eventually land on the asteroid.

    It has been revealed that at the time of the mission, the only instruments that could see the impact and the massive cloud of debris flying off Dimorphos were the Hubble Space Telescope and multiple telescopes on Earth. But they were unable to get a good enough view to see how much damage it did to the asteroid or any other potential changes that occurred.

    Sources indicate that this means that researchers had to estimate the damage until Hera highlighted scientists exactly what happened. Spoiler: All of those estimates were incorrect, and by a wide margin.

    Hera revealed the damage was vastly more significant than originally thought. Scientists believed the impact would generate a 20-meter crater; Hera found that almost the entire end of the asteroid had been blown off, resulting in a crater the size of a football stadium and as wide as Dimorphos itself. This is visible in the above image — as you can see, Dimorphos used to be roughly the shape of an egg. Now, it’s the shape of a deviled egg or a kidney bean, depending on which angle you view it from.

    The ESA’s Hera team discovered another neat effect of the impact: Before DART crashed into the asteroid, it was tidally locked to Didymos, much like the moon is to Earth. Scientists expected it to stay that way after the impact, but the images from Hera confirmed that Dimorphos now tumbles randomly, which none of the researchers had on their bingo card.

    In a recent development, “Before the DART impact, Dimorphos has always shown its same face to Didymos,” said ESA Hera Mission Specialist Michael Kueppers during the presentation. “And this is what we see now. You can see it looks for a few seconds in the video like regular rotation, but it’s spinning around completely crazy.”.

    ESA mission manager Ian Carnelli noted this surprise was great news because it’ll allow Hera to view Dimorphos on all of its sides, which would have been challenging if it were still tidally locked to Didymos.

    The ESA concluded the stream with one final surprise. According to Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, the Hera team told engineers that it was entirely safe to go to Dimorphos because all the debris would be ejected from the DART impact, with the remaining bits reabsorbed by Didymos and Dimorphos before Hera arrived.

    It has been revealed that but there is actually quite a lot of debris around the two asteroids. Kueppers indicates they’ve identified over 100 boulders so far, marked as white dots in the image above. Despite being completely wrong about the debris field, the Hera team was in good spirits since this means there are more things for the team to study.

    Sources indicate that kueppers says scientists are “always happy” either way because when they predict something correctly, they get awarded, and when they predict something wrong, they have a challenge to solve. “The problem is for the engineers,” he noted.

    The three discoveries were made just 20 days into Hera’s mission, which is slated to last six months. The Hera team said more images and discoveries are coming in the next half year.

    Sources indicate that the point of the DART mission was to see whether humans could deal with a potentially dangerous asteroid by ramming into it or destroying it, as is often seen in Hollywood films like Deep Impact and Armageddon. NASA even frames it as a “planetary defense test.”.

    According to recent reports, the mission was considered an overwhelming success. NASA was hoping to shorten the orbit of Dimorphos by at least 73 seconds, with the most optimal guess being approximately 10 minutes. The orbit was shortened by 33 minutes and 15 seconds. It was such a large discrepancy that scientists studied it and determined that the large amount of debris created extra recoil that amplified the push.

    According to recent reports, the change in orbit around Didymos also changed the orbit of both asteroids around the sun by about 11.7 microns per second. This doesn’t seem significant, but it adds up to about 1 kilometer every 2.7 years. This is enough to steer potential city-killer asteroids away from Earth’s orbit, given enough time and a significant enough battering ram.

    According to recent reports, hera’s findings also show the impact was much more devastating than scientists first thought. This provides even more data for NASA and the ESA to work through to proposal for such an event if it ever happens.

    “As newly introduced data come in each day, astronomers will be able to better assess whether, and how, a mission like DART could be used in the future to help protect Earth from a collision with an asteroid if we ever discover one headed our way,” said Lori Glaze, director of NASA’s Planetary Science Division, in a statement from 2022.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer.
    • Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.
    • Anthropic first released artifacts in 2024.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer. The “install as app” feature is available in beta for all free and paid Claude plans and works on both Mac and Windows, but not Linux.

    Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

    Anthropic first released artifacts in 2024. Since then, they’ve become a way to standardize and repeat tasks consumers do regularly, especially at work. Previously, artifacts ran via your Claude window or in a browser. By splicing them out as distinct desktop apps, you can now run different Claude queries while also using your artifacts locally, or use those apps without opening Claude at all.

    It has been revealed that “When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer,” Anthropic mentioned.

    Artifact apps can still access Claude and any connectors you’re using, and they upgrade automatically when you edit the artifact itself in Claude. When apps request something from Claude, though, that goes toward your Claude usage limits, which are lowest for free users.

    Anthropic noted the app feature is meant to streamline building apps for both developer and non-developer work.

    Also: Can AI initiative terrorist attacks? US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok.

    The revision clarifies where AI software for work is headed. Claude is already more of an AI-powered work suite than a single helpful chatbot for many organizations. Evidently, people are using tools like artifacts frequently enough — and simultaneously with other Claude features — that they need those Claude-based tools to function like discrete bits of software on their own.

    “If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention,” Anthropic stated.

    It has been revealed that claude artifact apps don’t have the same functionality as apps you could build using Claude Code, though. Even if you don’t need Claude open for these apps to work, you’ll still need to be signed in to Claude and have internet access, so they’re not an entirely portable or off-grid option.

    The feature’s support page also notes that legacy artifacts, “live artifacts from Claude Cowork,” and artifacts generated from templates like Docs, Slides, and Sheets can’t be installed as desktop apps.

    Sources indicate that first, make sure Claude for Mac or Windows is updated. You can try the “install as app” feature, which is in beta for all free and paid intends, via Claude’s Share menu. Select the Install as app option, which will then download the artifact you chose to your desktop. From there, set permissions as needed.

    Permissions range from the default (whatever they are in a browser) to app-specific permissions like sending notifications and full computer access.

    Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free.

    Sources indicate that full computer access means the artifact app can “run programs and read, change, or delete your files without asking each time,” Anthropic noted, so proceed carefully. Every time you edit and revision the artifact (and thus the app), Claude will ask you to confirm permissions again, so you’ll ideally have regular checkpoints to revise access. Still, there are some guardrails in place: Anthropic only lets you give full computer access to apps you’ve made yourself. For Team and Enterprise aims, that extends to any apps made by your coworkers.

    “Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust,” the manufacturer remarked.

    For Claude Enterprise plans, the install-as-app feature is off entirely until an admin turns it on in Organization settings.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Early in the second quarter Wednesday night in NBA Cup group play, LeBron James pulled up from Broad Street.

    He drilled a 35-foot 3-pointer amid a torrid stretch that saw him make a trio of triples and score 14 straight points for the 76ers on Thanksgiving Eve. Before that sequence, the Sixers were trailing the Miami Heat by three points at Philadelphia's Xfinity Mobile Arena. Afterward, they were up eight.

    It has been revealed that while becoming the oldest player in NBA history to notch a triple double — at 41 years and 330 days old — James continued his recent hot streak from beyond the arc, going 4 of 6 on 3-point attempts. Philadelphia shot 14 of 35 from long range en route to a 111-104 victory.

    The Heat (10-7) would have clinched East Group B had they come out on top, but Philadelphia (15-4) denied Miami an eighth consecutive win, despite losing Jaylen Brown to a hamstring injury late in the first half and Joel Embiid being sidelined by illness.

    Nick Nurse's squad is now 2-1 in NBA Cup competition; Erik Spoelstra's Heat dropped to that same mark.

    It has been revealed that james finished with a season-high 25 points and 12 assists, plus 10 rebounds, with maybe his most notable dime taking place early in the fourth quarter. The 22-time All-Star indicated his elite court vision, timing a halfcourt lob perfectly to connect with VJ Edgecombe for a layup. James later dialed up an alley-oop for forward Dominick Barlow to throw down.

    Edgecombe was among the Sixers players stepping up in the absence of Brown and Embiid, as Philadelphia protected its nine-point halftime lead and kept Miami at arm's length over the final two quarters. He had 18 points, and Tyrese Maxey poured in 30.

    The Heat, who wound up trailing by 16 late in the final frame, were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, who clocked out with 32 points, 14 rebounds and 4 assists.

    Sources indicate that kevin Durant is now one of five NBA players to score 33,000 points. The 38-year-old Houston Rockets forward achieved that feat on Wednesday night in a 116-104 home victory against the Phoenix Suns. He joined James, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Karl Malone and Kobe Bryant.

    Durant did so while piling up 20 points for Houston (14-5), which, despite already being eliminated from NBA Cup knockout-round contention, kept pace in the upper echelon of the Western Conference standings.

    The Rockets improved to 2-2 in Cup group play, while the Suns (9-8) slid to 1-2. They, too, have been eliminated from knockout-round contention in West Group A.

    Tech Report: Time Is Running Out for Apple’s iPhone Settlement. How to File a Claim Before Dec. 21

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (830 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The last day to file a claim in Apple’s $250 million settlement over delayed Siri features is Dec.
    • The class covers anyone in the US who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, the stretch when Apple was promoting a more personal Siri that hadn’t arrived yet.
    • The iPhone 16 went on sale in September 2024 with Apple Intelligence at the center of its marketing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The last day to file a claim in Apple’s $250 million settlement over delayed Siri features is Dec. 21, and payouts could reach $95 per eligible iPhone.

    The class covers anyone in the US who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, the stretch when Apple was promoting a more personal Siri that hadn’t arrived yet. Filing takes a few minutes online, and each qualifying phone gets its own claim.

    The iPhone 16 went on sale in September 2024 with Apple Intelligence at the center of its marketing. However, the first AI features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, several weeks later, and the most heavily promoted one, a Siri that could pull personal context from your apps, was further delayed in March 2025.

    Industry observers note that now you can turn that initial dismay into a payment in Apple’s $250 million legal settlement by signing up at a live website. The opt-in form is available only for a limited time, so get your name in the pool before it closes. Eligible buyers have until Dec. 21 to file, and each qualifying iPhone gets its own claim.

    Apple settled a false advertising lawsuit brought by Clarkson Law Firm in May, agreeing to pay $250 million to customers who bought some iPhone models during a specified period. The lawsuit alleged that Apple misled customers by promising AI features that didn’t ship with the upcoming devices. Apple denies all of the lawsuit’s allegations and denies that it did anything unlawful or improper.

    If you purchased an iPhone 16 or iPhone 15 at launch, you may be entitled to receive a portion of the quarter-billion-dollar settlement. Payouts between $25 and $95 per eligible device are expected.

    “Apple has reached a settlement to resolve claims related to the availability of two additional features. We resolved this matter to stay focused on doing what we do best, delivering the most innovative products and services to our customers,” an Apple spokesperson noted in an earlier statement to CNET.

    The court granted preliminary approval of the settlement on July 17. Then an Aug. 13 order moved up the final approval date by seven months.

    It has been revealed that “False advertising settlements aim to raise the floor of truth-telling, protect fair competition and increase consumer choice,” stated Ryan Clarkson, co-lead counsel on the case and founder and managing partner of Clarkson Law Firm, in a statement to CNET. He claimed it’s the largest false-advertising settlement in history.

    Apple lit up its flagship Latest York City store to resemble Siri’s new color scheme.

    In a recent development, as of Sept. 21, you can go to SmartphoneAISettlement.com and enter your information to confirm your eligibility for monetary relief. People whom Apple and the settlement administrator determined would be eligible will also receive email or postal notices from the company Verita directing them to the website.

    The claims window closes on Dec. 21, 2026, so you have three months to act.

    If you bought one of the following devices between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, you could be eligible to receive a settlement payment:.

    The iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max are included because they have the processor and memory to run Apple Intelligence features.

    It’s estimated that approximately 36 million customers are eligible for this settlement.

    When Apple advertised its fresh iPhone 16 lineup in 2024, it emphasized how the models were optimized for AI features such as an enhanced Siri that could act as an intelligent agent. When the phones did arrive, Apple Intelligence wasn’t yet ready; its first features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, five weeks later.

    According to the proposed settlement, “Apple allegedly saturated the market with deceptive ads, inducing consumers to purchase iPhones based on the promise of certain enhanced Siri features.”.

    It has been revealed that some features of Apple Intelligence did ship soon after the introduction of the iPhone 16 and iOS 18, including Visual Intelligence, Live Translation, Writing Tools, Genmoji and Clean Up. But those weren’t the advanced features Apple highlighted. In fact, the type of intelligent interactions Apple advertised is only starting to show up in Siri AI, which is part of iOS 27, which was released in early September.

    According to the settlement, Apple needed to provide the information about affected customers within five days of the settlement approval. As of late July, preliminary approval has been granted by the court.

    After the data is provided and verified, a 45-day notice period begins to inform potential consumers that they’re eligible for a payment.

    Recent findings suggest that on Aug. 13, US District Court Judge Noël Wise granted approval to push forward the date from Sept. 29, 2027, to Feb. 24, 2027.

    Provided approval is granted, the first checks or deposits will arrive sometime within a 60-day window after February next year, depending on court dates and possible extensions.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 11:05AM EST.
    • One important debate between Meta Platforms' (META +3.40%) bulls and bears is whether the tech giant's massive artificial intelligence (AI) spending is justified.
    • However, Meta Platforms' AI-related initiatives are slowly taking shape, and a recent partnership with Walmart (WMT -0.28%) highlights the opportunity ahead for the manufacturer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 11:05AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Meta Platforms ›.

    One important debate between Meta Platforms' (META +3.40%) bulls and bears is whether the tech giant's massive artificial intelligence (AI) spending is justified. The bears certainly have a point: The tech leader's free cash flow is declining, largely due to capex spending tied to its AI build-out. In the third quarter, Meta posted negative free cash flow of $2.1 billion, compared with positive free cash flow of $10.6 billion in the year-ago quarter.

    That's a significant decline. However, Meta Platforms' AI-related initiatives are slowly taking shape, and a recent partnership with Walmart (WMT -0.28%) highlights the opportunity ahead for the manufacturer.

    First, let's back up a little. Meta Platforms released its Muse AI agent to the public in early September. It quickly became one of the most downloaded iOS apps. Meta later released several other versions of Muse, including one for small businesses. Management noted on the firm's third-quarter earnings call that 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up Muse within a month and a half of its release. The tech giant also mentioned that 25% of those who had set up Muse used it daily, and growth remained strong.

    Sources indicate that but how does Meta plan to monetize Muse? The AI agent offers subscriptions for people who want higher usage capabilities (the base version is free). But Meta is targeting a potentially more lucrative opportunity. It plans to charge retailers transaction fees every time Muse helps a consumer make a purchase. That brings us to the manufacturer's partnership with Walmart. Meta Platforms and Walmart have partnered to integrate Muse with Walmart's e-commerce infrastructure through the retailer's Agent Gateway.

    The integration allows consumers to use Muse to discover products, compare prices, find deals, and complete purchases on their behalf, subject to user-defined permissions and spending limits. While the precise financial details of this deal were not disclosed, Meta could earn commission fees for transactions Muse helps facilitate.

    Recent findings suggest that walmart is one of the largest retailers in the world, so this partnership is an vital one for Meta. It could also help increase Muse's adoption. Some retailers are hesitant to get on board because they fear it will disrupt their business models and undermine their ability to protect customer relationships, as Meta's CFO, Susan Li, remarked.

    This may happen if agents like Muse become the primary shopping interface -- instead of visiting a retailer's website, consumers could ask an agent to compare prices, quality, and other factors across many retailers, thereby potentially reducing retailers' direct relationships with consumers. Even so, consumers' adoption will largely determine where this market is headed.

    It has been revealed that if Muse can continue gaining users, a significant percentage of them use the agent to make purchases, and at least some retailers start adapting to the change -- as Walmart is doing -- that could force other retailers to follow suit. Eventually, Meta could generate significant sales from transaction fees.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    It has been revealed that of course, Meta's core advertising business remains healthy. In the third quarter, the company's revenue increased by 26% year over year to $64.6 billion. It also ended the period with 3.64 billion daily active people, an increase of 3% year over year. Meta's AI-powered algorithms across its websites and apps have helped grow engagement.

    According to recent reports, as CEO Mark Zuckerberg pointed out, Facebook and Instagram are hitting near all-time highs in engagement, and Threads -- Meta's competitor to X (formerly Twitter) -- has overtaken X in monthly actives. The point is that even before we look at Meta's opportunity with Muse, the company's underlying business looks strong. It's also worth noting that building the capacity required to support an agent like Muse requires substantial upfront investments.

    Industry observers note that meta is dishing out that money today, but the company's expenses in this area should decrease over time, and as Muse gains traction, revenue growth, profits, margins, and free cash flow could jump. Lastly, Meta is trading at 16.3x forward earnings, which, in my view, is more than fair, considering the company's robust underlying business and long-term opportunities in advertising and AI.

    #131152. Industry News: The Winter Solstice Is Coming: A Guide to the Longest Night

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (809 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: The Winter Solstice Is Coming: A Guide to the Longest Night

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (809 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This was taken with the main camera as a ProRaw photo.
    • According to recent reports, thanksgiving is almost here, as is Cyber Monday, but soon it’ll be officially winter.
    • The winter solstice has a few different meanings, so here are all of them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This was taken with the main camera as a ProRaw photo. Notice the lights on the tree, compared to the green hue of the street lighting and blue and pink tones in the sky.

    According to recent reports, thanksgiving is almost here, as is Cyber Monday, but soon it’ll be officially winter. The winter solstice is on Dec. 21, when we’ll experience Earth’s shortest, darkest day.

    The winter solstice has a few different meanings, so here are all of them. The most common definition, and the one you’re most likely familiar with, is that it denotes the shortest day and longest night of the year on Earth. These times vary depending on your location on the globe, but the further north you live, the less sunlight you’ll get. In the tropics, they’ll get about 12 hours of sunlight. In Sweden, it’ll be closer to 6 hours. In Svalbard, there isn’t any.

    The reason this occurs is due to the second definition of the winter solstice: During this time, the North Pole is tilted as far away from the sun as it can get. According to The Farmer’s Almanac, the moment at which the Earth’s axis is physically tilted as much as it can be is at 3:50 p.m. ET on Monday, Dec. 21. After that moment, the process will begin to reverse until the South Pole takes its turn during the summer solstice. At that point, the North Pole will be at its closest tilt to the sun, giving us the longest day and shortest night of the year for the Northern Hemisphere.

    According to recent reports, sunset will occur at its earliest time on Dec. 21.

    According to recent reports, it’ll vary by location. The southern US will have the most sunlight, with Florida getting a little over 10 hours during the winter solstice. The Midwest and Great Lakes portion of the country will get roughly nine hours. The Pacific Northwest can expect a little less than nine hours. Southern Alaska will get about six hours, and the northern areas of Alaska will see around three hours.

    Sources indicate that if you want to see how your area will fare, Time and Date has a sunrise and sunset tool you can use. Input your zip code into the search bar, and you’ll be able to see your sunrise and sunset times.

    In a recent development, the city of Utqiaġvik, Alaska, will have it worse than most in the US: It won’t get any sun at all. The sun won’t rise there again until late January. We hope the people living there packed their vitamin D supplements.

    Recent findings suggest that the autumn equinox was just a couple of months ago, so you may be curious about the differences. A solstice occurs when the Earth’s poles are tilted as far away from the sun as they’ll be over the course of one year, which is also one orbit around the sun. The equinoxes take place at the halfway points between each solstice. The autumn equinox takes place in September between the summer and winter solstices, while the spring equinox takes place in March between the winter and summer.

    During an equinox, the poles are minimally tilted, and the days are as even as they can be. This also has a couple of other interesting side effects: The sun is pointed directly at the equator during an equinox, and the sun will rise and set directly east and west, respectively.

    Humans use the solstices and equinoxes to mark the change of the seasons. There are two equinoxes and two solstices, which mark the start and end dates for Earth’s four seasons.

    Decorating with evergreen trees, like with a wreath, is what they used to do to celebrate the winter solstice.

    While the solstice is close to the holidays, celebrations for the winter solstice have been around for significantly longer, and some winter solstice traditions have become Christmas traditions as well. One of the most historically famous winter solstice celebrations is Yule, a winter festival originating thousands of years ago among the ancient Norse. It became commonly celebrated in Europe and involved bonfires and massive feasts. Yule celebrations also included decorating with evergreen tree decorations, like holly and ivy.

    Recent findings suggest that if these sound familiar, it’s because Christmas co-opted many of those traditions centuries ago, and the two traditions have kind of merged into a single seasonal holiday. The terms Yule and Christmas are often used interchangeably these days in many cultures.

    So if you want to celebrate the winter solstice, just do all of the stuff you would normally do for the holidays. Burn a Yule log, decorate a tree, eat a major feast with your family and hang up mistletoe and wreaths — those are all hat tips to traditional winter solstice celebrations.

    Fast Fashion Fiasco: Shein to Pay $100 Million in FTC Complaint

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (419 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Shein, one of the biggest fast-fashion brands in the world, has been ordered to pay $100 million by the Federal Trade Commission, which alleges that the Singapore-based online retail giant engaged in deceptive practices that left millions of US customers dissatisfied with its products and policies.
    • The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase issues and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.
    • The complaint also alleges problems with the tech giant’s supply chain, false information about the origin of the cotton used in its clothes, a failure to communicate shipping updates to customers and a lack of support for those whose packages were late or went missing altogether.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shein, one of the biggest fast-fashion brands in the world, has been ordered to pay $100 million by the Federal Trade Commission, which alleges that the Singapore-based online retail giant engaged in deceptive practices that left millions of US customers dissatisfied with its products and policies.

    The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase issues and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.

    The complaint also alleges problems with the tech giant’s supply chain, false information about the origin of the cotton used in its clothes, a failure to communicate shipping updates to customers and a lack of support for those whose packages were late or went missing altogether.

    “The manufacturer misled millions of consumers about its products, its suppliers and the authenticity of its customer reviews,” Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection, noted in a statement on Tuesday.

    Shein has ballooned over the past decade into the ultra-fast-fashion brand we know today, thanks in large part to the impact influencers have had on social media, posting videos trying on clothing supplied by the company.

    In 2026, the organization is estimated to ship roughly 1 million packages to US customers daily, according to the FTC. That number becomes even more astounding when you consider that Shein, the FTC alleges, employed just five customer service agents to answer calls from American customers.

    This isn’t the first time Shein has faced negative scrutiny. Over the years, the company has faced allegations of numerous workers’ rights violations and is the largest polluter in the fast-fashion industry.

    In a recent development, according to Yale Climate Connections, the manufacturer emitted 16.7 million total metric tons of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere in 2023. Comparatively speaking, that’s more than the pollution output of four coal power plants. Shein has since pledged to improve its treatment of workers and reduce carbon emissions, but scrutiny persists.

    The $100 million will be used to compensate customers. And according to the FTC’s proposed order, the company, which earned roughly $50 billion in revenue in 2025, will not be able to continue advertising inaccurate shipping and delivery times; negative reviews will no longer be hidden; and its customer service offering will be bolstered.

    “The agreement does not constitute an admission of liability, and we continue to disagree with aspects of the FTC’s characterization of our business and compliance practices,” a Shein spokesperson told CNET.

    #131148. Black Friday Porch Pirates Don’t Care About Your Doorbell Camera. Follow This Expert Plan Now
