    Black Friday Porch Pirates Don’t Care About Your Doorbell Camera. Follow This Expert Plan Now

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1251 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Doorbell cameras may seem like a good way to make a porch thief think twice, but the reality doesn’t quite match up.
    • That’s the case for my fellow CNET editor, Gael Cooper, who had her Amazon delivery stolen a few weeks ago and spotted the thief on camera.
    • “When Amazon emailed me that the order was delivered and it wasn’t there, I was very confused,” Cooper said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Doorbell cameras may seem like a good way to make a porch thief think twice, but the reality doesn’t quite match up. Some porch pirates don’t care about being caught on camera as long as they’re able to steal your package, and it’s unlikely that law enforcement will track down the stolen goods.

    That’s the case for my fellow CNET editor, Gael Cooper, who had her Amazon delivery stolen a few weeks ago and spotted the thief on camera. It wasn’t expensive tech or a snazzy holiday gift — it was $36 worth of soda.

    “When Amazon emailed me that the order was delivered and it wasn’t there, I was very confused,” Cooper said. “When I pulled up the Ring footage, I saw the delivery happen on video, but then, 10 minutes later, a man in a blue hooded coat who’s intentionally hiding his face demonstrates up and grabs the box.”.

    In a recent development, package theft cases like this happen year-round, with CNET findings showing that 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or have stopped an attempted theft. And experts predict more stolen packages during the holidays, when thieves expect more deliveries.

    Recent findings suggest that so, don’t give thieves a chance. Now’s the time to make a blueprint to keep your Black Friday and Cyber Monday packages out of sight. But what tactics actually work if doorbell cameras don’t? Here’s what you should know about porch piracy and how to lessen your chances of package theft.

    Cooper’s Amazon order was scheduled to arrive between 3 a.m. and 6 a.m. — when it’s dark, but she knew she would be home. But thieves were already out lurking during those hours. Cooper noted the thief followed the driver and stole the package. She saw the thief stealing the package on her Ring security camera system.

    Greg Zakowicz, Omnisend’s e-commerce and retail advisor, stated Cooper’s package-theft incident is fairly typical, unfortunately — especially during the holiday season.

    According to recent reports, “Thieves know as well as shoppers that orders increase during this time, and often, the packages are more likely to contain more valuable items,” mentioned Zakowicz. “Shoppers during this time look to take advantage of deep discounts for not only gifts but themselves, making the package a potential goldmine for thieves.”.

    Recent findings suggest that there are a few steps you can take to lessen the likelihood of porch piracy. Zakowicz recommends using options like in-store pickups, post office boxes, in-garage delivery or deliveries to your workplace.

    That advice is especially important for expensive tech you proposal to have delivered to your home unless someone will be there to grab the package immediately.

    “While it may be less convenient, it’s a small price to pay to not have the hassle of gifts and expensive items going missing at the busiest shopping time of the year,” stated Zackowicz.

    Industry observers note that also ask your retailers not to ship the item in the manufacturer’s packaging. Some retailers, like Amazon and Target, will clearly display this before shipping because it could be an easy hint for thieves to guess what it is — especially if it’s tech. Even though this won’t stop porch pirates from being curious about what’s in the box, it may make them think about the effort and risk versus the potential reward, Zakowicz said.

    If you want another option to have packages delivered to your home, consider scheduling your deliveries for a time you know you’ll be available. For instance, you can set up an Amazon Day to have all of your Amazon packages delivered at once so you can plan accordingly.

    CNET found that US adults have mixed feelings about how effectively security cameras deter porch pirates: 11% of US adults believe they don’t deter them, while 9% use security cameras to get proof — not prevent it.

    It has been revealed that regardless of your home security measures, don’t assume you’re safe from porch pirates just because you have a doorbell camera, and don’t use it as a means of keeping an eye on your package if you’re busy or not home. Instead, when you see motion detection, that’s a sign to grab it right away.

    “The most common misunderstanding is that having security cameras will prevent thieves from stealing packages,” stated Zakowicz. “Thieves are thieves because being caught is not their biggest worry. They also know porch piracy is not at the top of most officers’ day-to-day public service worries. Often, by the time the report is made, thieves are long gone.”.

    Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, thieves may find other ways to steal packages, since their tactics are constantly changing. If that happens to you, there are a few steps you should take right away.

    According to recent reports, file a police report of the incident first. Be prepared to share information, including a description of the thief, and the make and model of the vehicle, with the police and your community so they can be vigilant of the thief.

    In a recent development, but don’t get your hopes up that the thief will be caught. Zakowicz said it’s rare that porch theft cases get solved.

    Industry observers note that “Police aren’t necessarily dedicating resources to solving porch pirates who stole a latest stuffed animal or board game. However, it’s key for them to understand areas seeing an uptick in thefts, as they can be more alert to suspicious activity,” noted Zakowicz. And the retailer may request it.

    According to recent reports, after filing, Zakowicz says to report the theft to the carrier and retailer. Carriers may use the data to assess future likelihood of package theft incidents and it could help instruct delivery drivers to carefully hide packages. Retailers may also be able to assist with a replacement.

    According to recent reports, cooper filed a police report with her local police department, which allowed her to upload the Ring video of the theft and acknowledged receipt. She’s not expecting the thief to be caught, but figures that her report could possibly help in some way.

    “I live in a pretty safe neighborhood in Amazon’s own hometown, but their delivery trucks are on our street dropping off packages every day,” she said. “It’s got to be a banquet for hungry thieves.”.

    She reached out to her neighbors to tell them about the theft, and one reported that she, too, had had a package stolen a week earlier.

    Recent findings suggest that cooper indicates she did not intentionally choose the early-morning drop-off time, but it was the only time Amazon offered for her delivery. Since then, she’s seen Amazon try to offer that same time and has chosen not to order an item rather than be forced to use that dark, quiet delivery slot.

    Immediately after the theft, Amazon was less than helpful, routing her to an AI agent who said it understood the situation was upsetting but that it wouldn’t be able to do anything for four days. When she checked back, Amazon agreed to refund her for the item, but kept insisting on labeling the package as “missing” and asked her to report back if she “found” it.

    According to recent reports, “I hope the driver doesn’t get in trouble for a supposedly ‘missing’ package,” she remarked. “It unnerves me that she was being followed by a thief. Who knows how long he followed that truck and how many packages he scooped up?”.

    #131147. Eli Lilly Is Now Worth 7 Novo Nordisks. Here’s How the Gap Got So Wide.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Eli Lilly Is Now Worth 7 Novo Nordisks. Here’s How the Gap Got So Wide.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (765 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 26, 2026 at 11:20AM EST.
    • Eli Lilly's (LLY -1.09%) market cap is roughly $1.2 trillion as of this writing.
    • Given that Novo Nordisk was the first to market with its GLP-1 shot, how did Eli Lilly get so much bigger?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 26, 2026 at 11:20AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Eli Lilly ›.

    Eli Lilly's (LLY -1.09%) market cap is roughly $1.2 trillion as of this writing. Novo Nordisk's (NVO +1.64%) market cap is $172.5 billion. Both are very large companies, but Eli Lilly is roughly seven times as large as Novo Nordisk. All the same, they are the number one and two players in the GLP-1 weight-loss niche of the pharmaceutical sector.

    Given that Novo Nordisk was the first to market with its GLP-1 shot, how did Eli Lilly get so much bigger? The story is a mix of self-inflicted wounds, intense competition, and short-term investors on Wall Street who may be missing a long-term investment opportunity. Here's what you need to know.

    Industry observers note that novo Nordisk brought out its Wegoy/Ozempic GLP-1 weight-loss shot before Eli Lilly introduced Mounjaro/Zepbound. That should have given Novo Nordisk a big head start, but the company underestimated the intensity of demand. It couldn't produce enough of the drugs, which opened the market to generic competition more quickly than usual. When Eli Lilly introduced its own GLP-1 drug, Novo Nordisk was competing with both Mounjaro/Zepbound and generic versions of its own drugs at the same time. Adding to the problem was the fact that Mounjaro/Zepbound was more effective. It isn't hard to see why Eli Lilly quickly took the lead in this emerging drug niche.

    Industry observers note that eli Lilly hasn't looked back. Through the first nine months of 2026, Mounjaro revenues grew 89%, while Zepbound revenues increased by 56%. The two drugs now account for 65% of the tech giant's revenues. To be fair, that's a concentration problem, given that the patents protecting the two drugs will eventually expire.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Industry observers note that however, investors have taken heart in the fact that Eli Lilly is using the cash influx from its GLP-1 drugs to invest in its pipeline. Notably, management has specifically been broadening the drug maker's portfolio into latest treatment areas to create a more diversified business. Given the still-strong growth in the GLP-1 niche and the organization's expanding drug portfolio, investors have only gotten more and more upbeat about Eli Lilly's future.

    It has been revealed that novo Nordisk is definitely working from behind right now, attempting to catch up to the GLP-1 leader. And given the depressed stock price and lofty 4.5% yield, Wall Street doesn't seem convinced that it can make a comeback. And yet, Novo Nordisk was again first to market with its Wegovy GLP-1 pill, beating out Eli Lilly's Foundayo. Foundayo is not the same drug as Mounjaro/Zepbound, so it hasn't performed quite as well as the Wegovy pill. In fact, the Wegovy pill has seen even stronger demand than Novo Nordisk's GLP-1 shots. This time, however, Novo Nordisk is making sure it can adequately supply the market.

    Recent findings suggest that there's just one small problem. Despite the success of the pill, the organization's financial results have been weak as it shifts to a low-price, high-volume model. Novo Nordisk appears to be making strong progress, given that it increased both its revenue and earnings guidance in the third quarter of 2026. But Wall Street is clearly in a show-me mood.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    According to recent reports, if you are a long-term dividend investor, however, the stock could be worth a look. Its lofty 4.5% yield is supported by a very strong 33% payout ratio. (For reference, Eli Lilly's yield is a tiny 0.5%.) And Novo Nordisk is clearly still an innovative drugmaker, given its head start with both a GLP-1 shot and a pill.

    In a recent development, if you want to buy an industry leader, Eli Lilly is clearly a firm you should look at in the pharmaceutical sector. However, the average pharma stock's price-to-earnings ratio is roughly 27x, and Eli Lilly's is 44x. Meanwhile, Novo Nordisk's P/E is just under 10x. If valuation matters to you, Novo Nordisk may be more attractive, and even if it isn't, Eli Lilly could still be too expensive for your tastes.

    • Recent findings suggest that etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two new credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

    In a recent development, the two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

    In a recent development, they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

    Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

    The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    According to recent reports, 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    Sources indicate that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    In a recent development, welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for newly introduced applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Industry observers note that elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

    You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

    The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    In a recent development, 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

    Recent findings suggest that welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

    According to recent reports, to maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

    Wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

    According to recent reports, travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

    The card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

    The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

    That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

    It has been revealed that with the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in Latest York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

    Bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

    If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

    However, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

    The earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

    That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

    Plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

    In a recent development, those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

    One of the most interesting perks of the latest cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

    There are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

    If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

    While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

    Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

    No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card.

    Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®.

    Luxury perks: American Express Platinum Card®.

    Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

    #131139. Latest Update: What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (699 w)
    📖 Baca
    EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
    • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
    • An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

    The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

    A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

    According to recent reports, an interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any complications are documented.

    In a recent development, A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

    Service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic issues that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

    Inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

    According to recent reports, detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

    Reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

    The good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

    However, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

    All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

    Some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

    However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

    Some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

    Reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

    Reddit people are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

    Car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several consumers suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

    Stock-Split Watch: 3 Industrial Stocks That Could Split in 2027

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that 10 stocks we like better than W.W.
    • Some investors, particularly those new to the game, like the idea of forward stock splits (the good kind of split) because they're getting more shares of the stock in question.
    • In a recent development, in reality, forward stock splits don't alter a company's overall market value.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Todd Shriber – Nov 26, 2026 at 11:45AM EST.

    Industry observers note that 10 stocks we like better than W.W. Grainger ›.

    Some investors, particularly those new to the game, like the idea of forward stock splits (the good kind of split) because they're getting more shares of the stock in question.

    In a recent development, in reality, forward stock splits don't alter a company's overall market value. That corporate action merely lowers the share price to make it more accommodating to a broader swath of market participants.

    It has been revealed that as nice as it is when companies do that, the frequency with which corporations are engaging in forward splits has been declining since the early 1980s. Blame the advent of fractional shares and the increased catering to institutional investors, who aren't price-sensitive.

    According to recent reports, stock splits aren’t a sure thing, but these three industrial stocks could make the move in 2027. Image source: Getty Images.

    In the first half of this year, fewer than 40 companies engaged in forward share splits. But hope always burns on this front, and there's nothing like four-figure or high triple-digit price tags to stoke the flames of a stock split.

    So, with that in mind, Deere (DE +4.44%), Transdigm Group (TDG +1.90%), and W.W. Grainger (GWW +1.28%) are three industrial stocks that may be primed for share splits in 2027.

    According to recent reports, among credible split candidates, W.W. Grainger isn't the most glamorous or most popular name, but it warrants a place in the split conversation. For example, the stock's Monday, Nov. 23 closing price of $1,390.12 is the second-highest among all industrial stocks, trailing only conglomerate Seaboard.

    Likely more instructive than that is the fact that Grainger has a history of splitting. It has undergone five 2-for-1 splits since 1970. The rub is that the last one occurred in June 1998, suggesting this industrial parts supplier may not be prioritizing share splits and that 2027 may come and go without one.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    In a recent development, with or without a move to lower its share price to woo more retail investors, Grainger offers other sources of appeal. Those include wide-moat positioning in the industrial and factory products supply space and its status as a Dividend King, or one of the companies that have raised dividends for at least 50 consecutive years.

    Like Grainger, Deere, one of the largest industrial companies, at least has a history of stock splits. The agricultural machinery giant has done so four times since 1972, though its last split occurred in December 2007.

    Deere's number of splits is comparable to that of other industrial companies. Likewise, these moves are a reminder of the value of long-term investing because market participants who bought just one share of Deere before the September 1972 split would have 24 shares today.

    Sources indicate that to be sure, there is no fixed price at which a manufacturer considers or is obligated to split its shares. But with a Monday, Nov. 23 closing print of $633.03, Deere is merely the 11th-most expensive industrial stock in dollar terms.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    That doesn't mean Deere won't announce a forward split next year. The tech giant may look to broaden its investor base, boost liquidity, or signal confidence in its growth projections. Still, ultimately, split hunters need to consider Deere a wait-and-see proposition.

    According to recent reports, just as there is no fixed price at which companies are more likely to mull splits, there is no such thing as an "overdue" split, and that wisdom is worth remembering as it relates to Transdigm. The purveyor of components and parts found on nearly every commercial and military aircraft worldwide, Transdigm celebrated its 20th anniversary as a public manufacturer in March. Over those two-plus decades, it's never split its shares.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    That brings us to today, well, Monday, Nov. 23, when the stock closed at $1,158.65 -- a price exceeded by just three other industrial stocks. Given its lack of split history, it's possible that Transdigm isn't actively evaluating a split to make its share price more accommodating.

    On the other hand, splits have to start somewhere, but that thesis is rooted in a lot of hope and not much else.

    Looking ahead to 2027, if investors are going to bet on anything with Transdigm, the safe wager is that the firm will remain acquisitive. Estimates vary, but Transdigm has made dozens upon dozens of acquisitions since its founding in 1993, and CEO Michael Lisman recently noted the company has "substantial M&A firepower...in excess of $10 billion.".

As a result, management reported that latest customers who returned to Reddit are up 50% year over year in Q3, indicating its efforts are working.

    In a recent development, the transition away from a dependence on search engines will take time, and in the interim, its shares may experience higher volatility.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the Pittsburgh Steelers are feeling good about their decision-making following the fallout from Aaron Rodgers' appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday.
    • While it was overall a pretty awful day for the team, Steelers owner Art Rooney II expressed optimism Thursday, saying he has "100 percent confidence in Mike McCarthy," via an interview with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette.
    • Rooney also spoke about the decision to release Rodgers, saying the quarterback was not being a "good teammate" when he publicly aired the team's grievances following his benching, per the Post-Gazette.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the Pittsburgh Steelers are feeling good about their decision-making following the fallout from Aaron Rodgers' appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday. Rodgers was promptly released from the team and head coach Mike McCarthy was retained despite some scandalous accusations from his former quarterback.

    While it was overall a pretty awful day for the team, Steelers owner Art Rooney II expressed optimism Thursday, saying he has "100 percent confidence in Mike McCarthy," via an interview with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette.

    Rooney also spoke about the decision to release Rodgers, saying the quarterback was not being a "good teammate" when he publicly aired the team's grievances following his benching, per the Post-Gazette.

    "There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload," Rooney noted. "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure.".

    Then he added, "In general, I think, historically, what's in the locker room stays in the locker room. That's the way it's always been. That's the way it should be as far as I'm concerned.".

    Rodgers didn't take that track. Instead, the quarterback ripped his head coach relentlessly during an appearance on McAfee's show. Rodgers claimed McCarthy routinely fell asleep during meetings, led the team in a "1-2-3 Packers" chant and questioned the coach's physical health.

    Rooney addressed that final accusation, saying McCarthy is "as healthy as the rest of us." The owner added, "health is not an glitch.".

    Rooney then further continued to express support for McCarthy, saying the coach took criticism for changes Rodgers made during games, particularly in the red zone.

    Industry observers note that "The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called, particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had," Rooney said. "Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn't working.".

    Rooney then confirmed that Rodgers was released after trying to deliver an ultimatum to McCarthy. Rodgers reportedly mentioned he wanted to call offensive plays or be released. McCarthy told Rodgers he doesn't get to make those calls, and decided to bench the veteran with the intention of releasing him in the coming days. Rodgers apparently fast-tracked that release with his interview on Wednesday.

    The owner also expressed confidence in now-starter Mason Rudolph, saying the team was "excited and lucky" to have him step into the starting role.

    At 6-4, the Steelers are still very much in the playoff hunt in the AFC. And after everything that occurred Wednesday, it might take a playoff appearance to salvage McCarthy's tenure with the franchise.

    Rooney may have given the coach a vote of confidence, but Rodgers' words will be tough to ignore if the team continues to struggle on the field.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The past six weeks have been tough for Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) and its shareholders.
    • In early November, the mid-term election results revealed a clear rebuke of massive data centers and the potential for increased regulations to slow development.
    • Sources indicate that the end result is a stock well off its all-time high, despite having just reported third-quarter revenue and earnings growth that both exceeded 100%.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Levy – Nov 26, 2026 at 12:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    The past six weeks have been tough for Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) and its shareholders. In October, growing concerns about how businesses will finance future build-outs for artificial intelligence (AI) started weighing on semiconductor stocks.

    In early November, the mid-term election results revealed a clear rebuke of massive data centers and the potential for increased regulations to slow development. And, of course, Jensen Huang's affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two employees ultimately led to his temporary resignation, leaving Nvidia without a permanent CEO for 11 days.

    Sources indicate that the end result is a stock well off its all-time high, despite having just reported third-quarter revenue and earnings growth that both exceeded 100%. CFO and interim-CEO Colette Kress mentioned it's "business as usual" at Nvidia, painting an optimistic picture on the company's earnings call. So, with the stock trading at a level rarely seen in the past year, should investors consider buying the stock? Warren Buffett's long-held investment philosophy can provide the answer to that question.

    According to recent reports, warren Buffett. Image source: Getty Images.

    Recent findings suggest that many investors might look at Nvidia's drop and think, "The market is fearful; I should get greedy." After all, Kress just increased her guidance for fiscal 2028 revenue growth from 70% to 75%. Wall Street analysts see Nvidia's earnings per share climbing above $16 next year. The stock trades at ridiculously low multiples.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Recent findings suggest that while it's true that Buffett has long noted that one of the keys to his success as an investor is "to be greedy only when others are fearful," that's not the only requirement for a good investment. Buffett also only invested in stocks when he had a high degree of confidence in their future. If a manufacturer was deemed too difficult to understand or forecast, he stayed away.

    According to recent reports, "Investors should remember that their scorecard is not computed using Olympic-diving methods: Degree-of-difficulty doesn't count," Buffett wrote in his 1994 letter to Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.54%) (BRKB +0.37%) shareholders. "If you are right about a business whose value is largely dependent on a single key factor that is both easy to understand and enduring, the payoff is the same as if you had correctly analyzed an investment alternative characterized by many constantly shifting and complex variables.".

    At this point, Nvidia's business is more like the latter than the former. Huang's actions and the potential repercussions leave many unanswered questions for investors. The high level of uncertainty about Nvidia's future explains why it trades at such a low multiple. It's not fear; it's a rational response to the recent events impacting the firm.

    There are a couple of alternatives to Nvidia stock trading at earnings multiples that aren't much higher than the chip leader.

    Sources indicate that buffett himself initiated a position in Alphabet (GOOG -2.02%) (GOOGL -2.13%) in 2025. His thesis was based on the company's ability to deploy huge sums of capital with a high return on investment. Specifically, Buffett was talking about its Google Cloud Platform and its data centers full of GPUs and custom silicon.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Industry observers note that alphabet is well-positioned to deliver high returns on invested capital in Google Cloud because of its full-stack approach to AI. It designs the systems and chips in its data centers; it offers a full cloud platform for developers (not just infrastructure); it develops a frontier large language model; and it integrates AI capabilities across its products.

    In a recent development, google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian mentioned that its payback period for the average server in its data centers is just two years, and its custom Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) systems break even within half that time. With a useful life of six years and a good operating margin, that's an exceptional return on invested capital. That return on invested capital is set to climb as more spending shifts from data center shells to revenue-generating servers.

    According to recent reports, another manufacturer positioned to grow based on a single key factor is Broadcom (AVGO -0.07%). Broadcom is the leading custom AI accelerator design partner, the one Alphabet uses for most of its TPUs. Growing demand for custom silicon, which costs less up front than GPUs and offers better price-performance, should result in its AI chip revenue climbing faster than the competition's for years to come. Its lead is protected by its intellectual property and its close relationship with its foundry partner, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Recent findings suggest that while Nvidia presently trades around 16 times earnings expectations, Broadcom's stock price isn't much higher at 17 times forward earnings. Alphabet is more expensive at 21 times forward earnings, but it's arguably the least risky of the group, considering its digital advertising business remains a huge cash cow funding its growth.

    Tech Report: What Are Repositioning Cruises?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1059 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
    • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
    • Industry observers note that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

    Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

    Industry observers note that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

    One key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

    This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

    It has been revealed that another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

    Just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a latest region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

    Industry observers note that repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit important sites when off the ship.

    If there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

    It has been revealed that for ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy shows, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

    Industry observers note that many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

    If you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

    Recent findings suggest that you can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

    Keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

    It has been revealed that here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

    This journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

    Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between New York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

    Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

    It has been revealed that departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

    It has been revealed that if Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and Latest England before reaching the Significant Apple.

    Departing Bergen, Norway, on June 11, 2027, this 28-night sailing aboard Viking Vela sails around Iceland's coast, makes two stops in Greenland and crosses the Atlantic before reaching Newly introduced York.

    Alphabet Could Be the Safest Way to Own Anthropic. Here’s the Math.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that it didn't take long for some of the early enthusiasm surrounding Anthropic (ANT +1.08%) stock to wear off.
    • Tech IPOs have a history of volatility, and it's particularly difficult to put a valuation on a company growing as quickly as Anthropic.
    • But there's another way to invest in the tech giant that developed Claude.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Patrick Sanders – Nov 26, 2026 at 12:27PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Alphabet ›.

    Sources indicate that it didn't take long for some of the early enthusiasm surrounding Anthropic (ANT +1.08%) stock to wear off. Shares of the artificial intelligence (AI) company opened at $111.50 on their first day of trading on Nov. 19, but fell below their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83 on just the fourth day of trading.

    I'm not surprised. Tech IPOs have a history of volatility, and it's particularly difficult to put a valuation on a company growing as quickly as Anthropic.

    But there's another way to invest in the tech giant that developed Claude. And the more I look at the numbers, the more I like the idea of buying Alphabet (GOOG -2.02%) (GOOGL -2.13%) stock instead.

    Alphabet has a sizable ownership stake in Anthropic, and it's also well positioned to earn tens of billions of dollars by leasing computing capacity to the AI lab.

    Recent findings suggest that at the time of this writing, Anthropic has a market cap of about $1 trillion. That puts the value of Alphabet's 13.7% ownership stake in it at $137 billion. Every time Anthropic gains $100 billion in market cap, Alphabet's investment increases by $13.7 billion, assuming the tech stalwart doesn’t sell any of its shares.

    If Anthropic grows into a $2 trillion tech giant, Alphabet's stake would be worth $274 billion. And if Anthropic becomes a $3 trillion company, Alphabet would be sitting on an investment worth $411 billion.

    Sources indicate that alphabet only becomes a stronger, wealthier company as Anthropic grows. That's a nice position to be in. And it doesn't even factor in that Anthropic also will be paying a lot to Google Cloud for its services.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Anthropic's S-1 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission revealed that the organization is committed to spending at least $121.3 billion for Google Cloud services between April 2026 and July 2033.

    That works out to roughly $16.7 billion annually over the life of the agreement, although the actual payments won't necessarily be spread out evenly over those years.

    In a recent development, what's particularly attractive about this agreement from Alphabet's perspective is that Anthropic is obligated to pay for the contracted computing capacity regardless of how much it actually uses. If Anthropic's needs fall short of its commitment, it generally still has to pay Google the difference, subject to certain contractual adjustments and exceptions.

    And that's only part of the business relationship.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic also estimates that it will spend another $125 billion to $150 billion for additional computing capacity powered by Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). They are the custom AI chips that Alphabet designs in conjunction with Broadcom (AVGO -0.07%).

    According to recent reports, anthropic can obtain that computing capacity directly from Google or through third-party providers. We don't know how much of that money will end up in Alphabet's coffers, and the payments depend on several factors, including how much capacity is made available.

    But Alphabet has an opportunity to do considerably more business with Anthropic than the $121.3 billion commitment suggests.

    There's an vital distinction between investing in Anthropic and doing business with Anthropic.

    The AI tech giant generated $17 billion in revenue in the third quarter, but it has also committed to spending approximately $900.9 billion, nearly all of it related to computing and infrastructure.

    Anthropic needs to generate enough revenue from Claude to justify those expenditures. Alphabet, meanwhile, is being paid to provide some of that infrastructure.

    In a recent development, and most importantly, Alphabet isn't entirely dependent on Anthropic for its success. It has its own AI platform, Gemini, a fast-growing cloud computing business that serves customers beyond Anthropic, and a highly profitable advertising business built around Google Search.

    I think Anthropic could be an outstanding manufacturer over the next decade, but I'm much less certain about what its stock will do in the next year or two.

    That's why I like Alphabet stock here. Anthropic could be a disappointing investment for its shareholders yet remain an extremely valuable customer for Google Cloud. I don't need to get Anthropic's valuation right to make money by owning Alphabet stock.

    Here's What Would Prove Me Wrong About Netflix Stock

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (820 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This month, I've argued Netflix (NFLX +0.92%) stock is worth buying near $60, mostly because the streaming giant's profits keep rising even as its sales growth cools.
    • At $59.41, shares sell for around 16 times earnings, using analysts' average estimate for 2027.
    • Recent findings suggest that but what would prove me wrong?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 26, 2026 at 12:41PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Netflix ›.

    This month, I've argued Netflix (NFLX +0.92%) stock is worth buying near $60, mostly because the streaming giant's profits keep rising even as its sales growth cools. The shares ended Wednesday, Nov. 25, at $59.41. That put them just over their Nov. 20 close of $56.73, the lowest since May 2024, and about 56% under their highest close ever, $133.91 on June 30, 2025 (adjusted for last year's 10-for-1 split).

    At $59.41, shares sell for around 16 times earnings, using analysts' average estimate for 2027. In comparison, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) was at 17.1 times forward earnings, according to a Nov. 20 FactSet report.

    Recent findings suggest that but what would prove me wrong? Any one of three things would: total view hours (the time members spend watching) down from a year earlier, 2027 ad revenue below $3 billion, or a 2027 operating margin target under 32%. Each would suggest a weaker business than the price assumes.

    Much of the streaming service's growth comes from hiking prices, which usually works only while members keep watching. They still are. In the first half of 2026, members watched more than 97 billion hours on Netflix, up 2% year over year and a bit faster than the 1.5% gain in all of 2025.

    Members also took this year's price hikes much as they took past ones, management said in October.

    Sources indicate that but 2% is slow growth, and management knows it. In its third-quarter shareholder letter, Netflix acknowledged "some investor concern about our view hours growth" and remarked it wants to speed up that growth.

    According to recent reports, the next test is in the first quarter of 2027, when Netflix looks to change its viewing report from every six months to once a year. If that report indicates total view hours lower than a year before, I'd read it as a sign that members are watching less while paying more. That might make future price hikes tougher to push through.

    Advertising was supposed to become Netflix's other significant growth engine, and it's taking longer than planned. Ad revenue climbed more than 150% in 2025, to over $1.5 billion, and in January, management expected it to roughly double this year. In October, Netflix mentioned it now expects around $2.7 billion instead, because some of its ad features have rolled out a bit more slowly than planned.

    Recent findings suggest that even $2.7 billion would be fast growth, just slower than 2025's rate and the original blueprint. And Netflix prepares to launch its ad-supported tier in 15 more countries in 2027, starting with 12 of them in March.

    Recent findings suggest that my bar is the $3 billion Netflix first expected for this year. If 2027 ad revenue can't top that level, even with another year plus 15 new countries, I'd see the glitch as more than a slow rollout.

    My case leans hardest on Netflix's operating margin. Management expects it to reach 31.5% in 2026, up from 26.7% in 2024, and notes that implies operating income growth of over 20% this year. This widening margin is a major reason earnings per share can keep climbing faster than sales.

    "[O]ur intent is to grow our operating margin each year," the firm wrote in its January shareholder letter, adding that the size of each year's rise will vary.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Sources indicate that even my more cautious forecasts assume the margin improves by half a point a year. That makes Netflix's 2027 margin target, which management says it'll share in January, the figure I'll watch most closely. A target under 32% might mean Netflix must spend more just to keep growing. And it would leave my earnings forecasts for the next few years too high.

    Recent findings suggest that debt isn't on my list. Netflix finished September with net debt (debt minus cash) of around $7.1 billion, under half the operating income it expects this year.

    None of the three has happened. View hours are still climbing, ad revenue should still jump this year, and Netflix still expects its operating margin to hit 31.5%.

    For now, my case stands, and at roughly $59 I think the growth stock is still worth a look. But if Netflix's fourth-quarter report includes a 2027 margin target below 32% or an ad revenue forecast under $3 billion, I'd need to rethink that.

    By Harsh Chauhan – Nov 26, 2026 at 12:57PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    In a recent development, nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) has been hammered on the market lately. Even a strong set of quarterly results from the company earlier this month couldn't change investor sentiment, before the reinstatement of co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO sparked a massive rally earlier this week.

    However, investors will do well to look past the noise and focus on the company's financial performance. Nvidia easily beat Wall Street's expectations for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 (which ended Oct. 25). The company's guidance clearly indicates that its incredible growth is sustainable, driven by the data center business that played a central role in boosting its revenue and earnings last quarter.

    However, there is another segment that's starting to move the needle for the company, and I won't be surprised to see this business becoming massive over the next decade.

    According to recent reports, data centers have been at the forefront of the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution so far. However, the technology is now moving from data centers into the real world. Physical AI -- the integration of AI into machines and physical objects such as cars, drones, robots, factory equipment, medical equipment, and other devices -- is emerging as the next big growth driver for Nvidia.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Nvidia notes that its physical AI revenue almost tripled year over year in the previous quarter. What's more, Nvidia expects to generate $25 billion in physical AI revenue in fiscal 2027. That's a huge leap over fiscal 2026, when physical AI added $6 billion to Nvidia's top line. The company is on track to clock almost $424 billion in revenue for fiscal 2027, meaning physical AI will account for nearly 6% of its top line this year.

    According to recent reports, nvidia's incredible growth in physical AI isn't surprising, as it has been pushing the envelope in this space. Companies such as Caterpillar, Boston Dynamics, LG Electronics, and other robotics companies are using Nvidia's robotics solutions to develop AI-enabled robots. The semiconductor giant also offers a platform to help customers develop and deploy humanoid robots in healthcare, manufacturing, and retail.

    Industry observers note that it won't be surprising to see Nvidia's physical AI business become significantly bigger over the coming decade. Counterpoint Research estimates that cumulative physical AI shipments could reach 145 million units by 2035. Barclays estimates that the physical AI market could be worth $1.4 trillion in 2035, which means that Nvidia is scratching the surface of a massive growth opportunity.

    As such, there is a solid chance that Nvidia's physical AI revenue will grow at a solid clip over the next 10 years, complementing the growth of the company's data center business.

    In a recent development, nvidia stock is down 26% over the past month. As a result, investors can now buy it at just 16.7 times earnings. The forward earnings multiple of 9.3 is even more attractive for a manufacturer whose earnings are poised to double this year. Additionally, Nvidia has raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth estimate by five percentage points to 75%.

    Analysts have raised their earnings per share (EPS) expectations for the next couple of years, which isn't surprising considering that the organization is already sitting on a lucrative multi-year growth opportunity in AI data center infrastructure.

    NVDA EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts.

    Nvidia noted on the latest earnings call that the cloud industry's backlog now sits at a whopping $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion just three months ago. This huge backlog will ensure that hyperscalers and AI companies continue to invest in more chips, and that's great news for Nvidia considering that it controls 75% of the AI chip market.

    The emergence of additional catalysts, such as physical AI, could help Nvidia consistently beat Wall Street's expectations, improving investor confidence in the stock. So, even though Nvidia has taken a beating lately, its growth prospects are still solid. That's why opportunistic investors may consider capitalizing on this AI stock’s recent slide before it becomes a long-term winner.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Another day, another substantial swing.
    • In a recent development, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
    • Sources indicate that the amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Another day, another substantial swing. This one's lower, but don't count on it starting a trend: We keep seeing mortgage rates move back and forth, but no one's expecting rates to take a dive. If you're watching this space because you're waiting to refinance, it's unlikely your wait is about to end.

    In a recent development, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points lower than yesterday and unchanged from a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    Sources indicate that the amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising. Mortgage lenders' rates are never identical, but when we're seeing rapid change, the gaps between lenders tend to widen — and that's for sure what I saw. I looked at six different lenders, and saw a nearly 70-basis-point difference between the highest and lowest APRs. (And yes, that was looking for the same loan amount, location and so on.).

    According to recent reports, my point is, whether you're looking to buy or refinance, make sure to shop multiple lenders. You're the same candidate bringing the same financials to each one, but you could end up with extremely different rate quotes. And it pays to compare. Freddie Mac estimates that comparing at least two lenders could save you up to $600 per year in interest. Compare four or more, and that savings is over $1,200 annually.

    In a recent development, here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Sources indicate that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to upcoming inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Mortgage rates may be lower today, but like I mentioned above, it's been more of a seesaw than a ski slope — and we may be about to hit the high side again. The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out tomorrow morning. Recently, when rates have moved higher, inflation's been in the mix.

    In a recent development, strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

    Industry observers note that we already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three major inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI highlighted wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

    Industry observers note that predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Markets are currently anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.

    Industry observers note that but back to the upcoming holiday: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

    » Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you initiative to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.63% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

    Industry observers note that also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    Industry observers note that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    In a recent development, if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    According to recent reports, nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a newly introduced home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    Sources indicate that if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Five years after the death of John Madden, the NFL is keeping the memory of the broadcaster's connection to Thanksgiving alive.
    • The league unveiled last week that a Madden coin, featuring Madden's silhouette on one side and a six-legged "turducken" (a chicken stuffed in a duck, stuffed in a turkey) on the other, will be used for coin flips for the three NFL games on Thanksgiving Day.
    • In a recent development, all players in those games — Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears, Dallas Cowboys-Philadelphia Eagles and Buffalo Bills-Kansas City Chiefs — will wear patches on their uniforms with the Madden silhouette.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Five years after the death of John Madden, the NFL is keeping the memory of the broadcaster's connection to Thanksgiving alive.

    The league unveiled last week that a Madden coin, featuring Madden's silhouette on one side and a six-legged "turducken" (a chicken stuffed in a duck, stuffed in a turkey) on the other, will be used for coin flips for the three NFL games on Thanksgiving Day.

    In a recent development, all players in those games — Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears, Dallas Cowboys-Philadelphia Eagles and Buffalo Bills-Kansas City Chiefs — will wear patches on their uniforms with the Madden silhouette. The Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers, who played on Wednesday (or "Thanksgiving Eve," as the league calls it), also wore the patches.

    Stencils honoring Madden will be placed in the end zones and along the sidelines of the three home fields during the matchup, and panels on the stadium wall will feature Madden in his coaching days with the Oakland Raiders.

    Sources indicate that along with those Madden-themed additions, the MVP of each game will receive a trophy fashioned to look like a turkey leg-football amalgamation. The Thanksgiving MVPs will also earn a $10,000 donation from the NFL Foundation to a high school or youth football program in their name.

    Madden, one of the defining figures of the sport as both a coach and broadcaster, died in 2021 at the age of 85. Alongside longtime broadcasting partner Pat Summerall, Madden called NFL games for decades on CBS and later Fox, becoming associated with Thanksgiving games thanks to his enthusiasm for turduckens and turkey legs.

    The league first introduced the specialized Madden patches and coins in 2023, two years after the football legend's death, and have continued the tradition over the past few years.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education.
    • Sources indicate that grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses.
    • Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education. It’s free money you aren’t expected to pay back.

    Sources indicate that grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses. Some grants, depending on who awards them, require an application or have requirements you must meet before you can get your money.

    Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.

    There are four main types of grants:.

    Federal grants come from the federal government.

    State grants come from state programs and often can only be used at schools in that state.

    Institutional grants come from your college or university, or even your program or major.

    Private grants come from nonprofits, community organizations and individual donors.

    To receive a federal grant, you must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). Most states require the FAFSA for state grants, and a few require a separate state application. You’ll need to complete the FAFSA for each year you’re enrolled in school. You may need to meet certain eligibility requirements, such as income limits, to get some grants. The FAFSA is how you apply for the Pell Grant, which is a financial need-based grant. The FAFSA also determines eligibility for federal work-study, which is a job program rather than a grant.

    Federal aid, including federal grants, typically requires students to meet satisfactory academic progress. This means you have to maintain a minimum grade point average and be on track to finish your degree on time, as determined by your school. Your school also sets how many credits you must take to qualify for grant funding.

    Some grants — typically private or institutional grants — require an additional application that asks for transcripts, letters of recommendation and personal essays. Your school’s financial aid office or the grant provider will have details on applying for specific grants.

    After you submit the FAFSA, you’ll receive a financial aid award letter from each school you applied to, which outlines how much in federal, state and institutional grants you’ve been offered. You must accept your aid to receive it.

    In a recent development, most grants will be disbursed directly to your college or university. Your school will apply the grant money first to tuition, fees and any other charges it bills, such as housing or a meal initiative.

    In a recent development, in some cases, you may receive more grant money than your school bills, which is the best-case scenario. If that happens to you, any leftover funds will likely be refunded to you. Refund timelines vary by school, so it may take some time to get your money. You can get your refund faster by setting up direct deposit with your school. You can then use the funds for other costs approved by your grant — some examples are detailed below.

    If you have questions about your grant money, contact your college’s financial aid office.

    Grants can help cover cost-of-attendance expenses. Generally, you can use grant money to pay for tuition, textbooks, class materials, transportation, housing and food. Depending on your school’s policies, you can use grant money to cover summer classes or study abroad programs, too.

    Some grants come with specific terms about how you can spend them. Check your financial aid award letter or, for a private or institutional grant, the school’s or organization’s website to find specifics.

    Expenses grants aren’t meant for:.

    After your grant is applied to your tuition and school expenses, you can options to fill the gaps between what the grant covers and the total cost of your program. Some options include savings, scholarships, work-study, payment intends, federal student loans or, as a last resort, private loans. By using grants to pay for your college education, you may be able to borrow less.

    To maximize the grants you’re eligible to receive, enter accurate information on the FAFSA and complete it as soon as you can — some funds are first-come, first-served. Also, don’t limit yourself to federal or state grants — search and apply for as many privately funded grants as you can find.

    Your grant money usually goes straight to your college or university to pay your tuition and fees. Anything that is left over may be disbursed to you for other school-related costs.

    Yes, but it depends on your grant. Housing is part of your cost of attendance, so you can use grant money to pay for off-campus rent.

    You don’t have to pay back a grant as long as you continue to meet all requirements for the grant, such as staying enrolled. You can use grant money on school and school-related expenses. Some grants may require you to meet eligibility requirements such as a minimum GPA or state residency. If you receive more grant money than your cost of attendance for a given school term, ask your financial aid office if you can put that grant money toward next year’s cost of attendance.

    If you have a federal grant like a Pell Grant, these are examples when you may have to repay all or part of the grant:.

    You withdrew from your program.

    You received enough scholarship money to reduce your federal aid need.

    Recent findings suggest that it depends. You can usually use grant money to buy a laptop. Computers are considered course materials, which fall under cost-of-attendance expenses, so they can be covered by a grant. However, always double-check with the grant provider and your financial aid award letter to ensure that you’re following all restrictions. Whether you can use grant money to cover a laptop depends on your school’s policies and how much grant money you receive.

    According to recent reports, if you get more grant money than your school bills you, you’ll likely receive the leftover money to spend on other cost-of-attendance expenses. You can use this money on living costs such as transportation or housing. Grant money often goes mostly toward tuition, so a refund isn’t guaranteed.

    Grant and scholarship money is generally tax-free when you use it for tuition, required fees, books and required class supplies. If you have additional questions, consider talking to a tax professional.
